schemes.scheme_name: Mukhya Mantri Sahara Yojana
schemes.administering_body: Department of Health and Family Welfare / Himachal Pradesh Swasthya Bima Yojana Society; official portal says the scheme has shifted to ESOMSA
schemes.benefit_summary: Rs 3,000 per month for economically weaker Himachal residents suffering from specified serious/fatal or permanently incapacitating diseases, including Parkinson’s, malignant cancer, paralysis, muscular dystrophy, haemophilia, thalassemia, chronic renal failure and other qualifying conditions.
schemes.eligibility_text: Applicant must be a Himachal resident, economically weaker, suffering from a listed disease or another disease rendering the person permanently incapacitated, and not be a beneficiary of another government-sponsored pension scheme. The current official page does not publish one numeric income ceiling.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm the current economic-weakness/income threshold, medical-board definition, pension-overlap rule after transfer to ESOMSA and the live receiving-office workflow. Old portal registration/status links return session/404 errors in automated access.
schemes.exclusions_text: Non-Himachal residence, no qualifying disease/permanent incapacitation, inability to establish economic weakness, receipt of another government pension, false records or missing life/medical updates can exclude or stop assistance.
schemes.documents_required: Himachal residence/bonafide proof; Income or economically-weaker-section certificate; Medical records and competent-authority certificate; Bank details; Aadhaar/identity document; Passport photograph
schemes.conditional_documents: BPL certificate if used as local economic test; Disability/medical-board certificate; Life certificate and updated medical/income certificate; Additional records requested by ESOMSA/District Welfare Officer
schemes.application_mode: Previously online through the official SAHARA portal and offline through BDO/Panchayat; the current portal notice says the scheme shifted to ESOMSA, so confirm the receiving ESOMSA/District Welfare Office before filing.
schemes.application_steps: Collect residence, income/economic-weakness, medical and bank documents.; Check the ESOMSA/e-Kalyan or District Welfare Office route because the official portal announces the departmental transfer.; If the SAHARA portal accepts registration, upload the documents; otherwise submit the prescribed form through BDO/Panchayat/District Welfare Office.; Retain acknowledgement/application ID and track with the receiving department.; Update life, BPL/income and medical certificates when requested.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No fixed public deadline found. Continuation requires current life, income/BPL and medical verification; confirm renewal period with ESOMSA.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Old links include status, card, payment and certificate updates but several are currently broken. Escalate to ESOMSA/District Welfare Officer, HPSBYS support or Mukhya Mantri Sewa Sankalp 1100.

schemes.scheme_name: Indira Gandhi Sukh Suraksha Yojana (replaces Beti Hai Anmol Yojana from 1 April 2026)
schemes.administering_body: Directorate of Women and Child Development, Government of Himachal Pradesh; Child Development Project Officer (CDPO); designated insurance company
schemes.benefit_summary: For each of the first two eligible girls in a BPL Himachal family, the state deposits Rs 25,000 with an insurer in the girl’s name at birth. Parents/legal guardians receive group term life cover of Rs 2,00,000 per parent. Corpus plus accrued benefits is payable at age 18, with an option to defer to age 27.
schemes.eligibility_text: Family must be BPL and resident of Himachal Pradesh. Girl must be the first or second daughter, born on or after 1 April 2026, and parents/guardians must not already have used the replacement scheme for two daughters. The girl must not marry before age 18.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Final insurer, e-District service record, birth-application time limit, legal-guardian treatment and transition SOP are not yet clear. Gazette allows maturity at 18 or optionally 27 and says Director WCD may issue further SOP.
schemes.exclusions_text: Non-BPL/non-Himachal families, third or later daughters after two benefits, births outside the notified date, false records or marriage before 18 can exclude or forfeit benefits. Misuse may be recovered; girl’s death triggers the Gazette’s refund/reallocation safeguards.
schemes.documents_required: Girl child birth certificate; BPL certificate/card; Bonafide Himachali certificate; Aadhaar of girl and parents/guardian where available; Parent/guardian bank and identity details; Application form with first/second-daughter declaration
schemes.conditional_documents: Legal guardianship/relationship proof; Death/claim documents for an insured parent; Insurance account/claim documents at maturity or early-event claim; Additional family-register/birth proof requested by CDPO
schemes.application_mode: Apply after birth registration through e-District or a designated registration centre; CDPO verifies and sanctions, then WCD deposits the corpus and arranges insurance.
schemes.application_steps: Register the birth and obtain birth, BPL, bonafide and identity documents.; Open the e-District/designated-centre service and submit the form.; CDPO/field staff verify BPL, residence, birth date and first/second-daughter status.; After sanction, retain insurance-account/corpus and parental-cover details.; Track periodic statements and maturity/claim status through CDPO/WCD.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No annual deadline stated. Apply after birth registration for eligible births from 1 April 2026; account is tracked until 18 or 27 if deferred. Older eligible births remain under Beti Hai Anmol under the transition clause.
schemes.tracking_grievance: CDPO/District Programme Officer and Directorate WCD; district grievance cell, Women Helpline 181, Mukhya Mantri Sewa Sankalp 1100 and state committee escalation under Director WCD.

schemes.scheme_name: Mukhya Mantri Swavalamban Yojana (MMSY)
schemes.administering_body: Department of Industries, Government of Himachal Pradesh; District Level Committee and District Industries Centre; financing bank
schemes.benefit_summary: For bona fide Himachali youth aged 18–45: investment subsidy generally 25% of eligible plant/machinery and technical civil works, 30% for women, eligible plant/machinery ceiling Rs 40 lakh and total project cost up to Rs 60 lakh. Also 5% interest subsidy for three years on eligible loans up to Rs 40 lakh and CGTMSE fee reimbursement.
schemes.eligibility_text: Applicant must be bona fide Himachali youth aged 18–45 proposing eligible manufacturing, service, trade or shop activity, with viable project, financing appraisal/loan, at least 10% own contribution in the approval format, and DIC/District Level Committee compliance. Unit must start within six months for service/trade/shop or one year for manufacturing.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Detailed operational rules are from 2019 and the latest 2025-26 approval-direction PDF is poorly OCR’d and appears to contain a past cut-off. Confirm acceptance for FY 2026-27, current activities, ceilings, age and whether a newer startup scheme supersedes MMSY.
schemes.exclusions_text: Cash-paid plant/machinery is ineligible; land and consumables are excluded. Failure to start on time, physical verification, valid bank loan/own contribution, eligible activity/residence/age or duplicate incentive rules can defeat subsidy; DIC monitors units for three years.
schemes.documents_required: Aadhaar; Bonafide Himachali certificate; Project profile/business plan including land details; Bank appraisal and sanction letter; Own-contribution and project-cost details; Udyam/Udyog registration as applicable; Land/building and equipment quotations
schemes.conditional_documents: Loan account statement and bank physical inspection report; GST-valid supplier bills paid electronically; Undertaking and certified engineer certificate; CGTMSE and commercial-production certificate; Activity-specific licences
schemes.application_mode: Initial application online through the Department of Industries Single Window/MMSY portal; after DLC approval and loan disbursement, claim subsidy via financing bank to GM DIC.
schemes.application_steps: Confirm with DIC that MMSY accepts new cases in the current FY.; Prepare project profile, land, Aadhaar, bonafide certificate, costs and own contribution.; Register/apply on the official portal and obtain DLC in-principle approval.; Secure bank finance and establish the unit within the applicable period.; File subsidy claim through bank with sanction letter, electronic bills, inspection report, undertaking and engineer certificate.; DIC verifies and sanctions; retain records for three-year monitoring.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No reliable current deadline found; the latest official direction appears to reference a past 31 March 2025 cut-off. Initial application has no annual renewal, but interest/guarantee claims and monitoring are periodic.
schemes.tracking_grievance: MMSY/Single Window dashboards and concerned GM DIC; Department of Industries 0177-2625240, dirindus-hp@nic.in; portal has Query/Citizen Grievance dashboards.

schemes.next_review_action: Obtain FY 2026-27 MMSY notification or written DIC confirmation and update deadline, activities, ceilings and live status.

schemes.administering_body: Department of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Government of Himachal Pradesh, with LPG Oil Marketing Companies and Panchayat/Food Civil Supplies field verification
schemes.benefit_summary: Free domestic LPG connection for eligible Himachal households not covered by Ujjwala or another state/central LPG scheme. Official budget/plan material also describes free stove/cylinder/pipe for new beneficiaries and free refill support, but current refill count/timing needs confirmation.
schemes.eligibility_text: Any bona fide Himachal household with no domestic LPG connection in its own name or under any state/central sponsored scheme may qualify; official planning material says the scheme covers eligible households not covered under Ujjwala. Original inclusion also covered fire, flood, flash-flood or earthquake victims with competent revenue certificate; 2019 budget stated households without a female member could qualify if other conditions are met.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm whether current implementation is all no-connection households or a narrower BPL/poor test, whether any member’s connection disqualifies the family, and current refill/stove entitlement. The ePDS form link currently returns 404.
schemes.exclusions_text: Already having domestic LPG or a government-scheme connection excludes the household. Official scheme text also excludes households with a regular/contractual government/board/corporation/autonomous-body/bank/PSU/local-body employee, income-tax payer, registered government contractor or government pensioner; social-security pension is excepted. Exclusion prevails if both tests apply.
schemes.documents_required: Ration card/household record; Bonafide Himachali/residence proof; Aadhaar/identity details; Declaration of no domestic LPG and no Ujjwala/other LPG coverage; Bank details if subsidy/refill is DBT; Prescribed Grihini Suvidha form
schemes.conditional_documents: Tehsildar/SDM/DM disaster certificate; Income/BPL proof if local implementation applies targeted test; Pension, employment, contractor or income-tax status declarations
schemes.application_mode: Form-based through Food/Civil Supplies, Panchayat/Fair Price Shop/field channel or LPG distributor. Official ePDS Forms Center lists the form; Single Window lists an online service but not a direct live URL.
schemes.application_steps: Confirm no household member has an LPG connection and no Ujjwala/other government coverage.; Obtain the latest form from ePDS/Food Civil Supplies, Panchayat, Fair Price Shop or LPG channel.; Attach ration card, residence, Aadhaar/identity and no-connection declaration; add conditional evidence where applicable.; Submit to Panchayat/food-supply official or distributor for verification.; After approval, complete LPG KYC/connection formalities and ask about current free-refill entitlement.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No fixed application deadline found. Apply while the household has no qualifying connection; connection/refill support depends on current budget/entitlement.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Use ePDS/Food Civil Supplies office, Fair Price Shop/Panchayat, LPG distributor and ePDS grievance link. Single Window lists procedure/checklist but no direct live URL; escalate through Mukhya Mantri Sewa Sankalp 1100.

schemes.scheme_name: Himachal Pradesh Disability Relief Allowance (State Disability Pension)
schemes.administering_body: Directorate for Empowerment of SCs, OBCs, Minorities and the Specially Abled (ESOMSA), Government of Himachal Pradesh; Tehsil Welfare Officer and District Welfare Officer
schemes.benefit_summary: Rs 1,000/month for 40–69% permanent disability; Rs 1,500/month for 70% or more disability. Persons aged 70+ with disability receive Rs 1,500; official ESOMSA text also states no income limit for 70%+ disability and intellectual disability.
schemes.eligibility_text: Applicant must have a permanent disability certificate of at least 40% from a medical board constituted under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, have no adult children, and have total annual income from all sources not exceeding Rs 35,000. The official page removes the income ceiling for intellectual disability and 70%+ disability. Gram Sabha identifies/recommends; 70%+ applicants may apply directly to TWO/DWO.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Detailed ESOMSA text carries a last-revised 2021 date although the site is current in 2026. Confirm whether rates, Rs 35,000 ceiling, no-adult-child rule and age-70 treatment changed, and whether Him Access/e-Kalyan online filing is now mandatory.
schemes.exclusions_text: Disability below 40%, no permanent certificate, income above Rs 35,000 without exception, adult children where the rule applies, false documents or incompatible pension/benefit can exclude. Income and Gram Sabha recommendation are not required for stated 70%+ or 40%+ mental-disability exceptions, but DWO may seek identity/bank evidence.
schemes.documents_required: Permanent disability certificate from competent medical board; Himachal residence/bonafide proof; Income certificate unless exempt; Parivar register/family record and adult-child evidence; Aadhaar/identity; Bank account/passbook; Prescribed social-security pension form; Gram Sabha/Panchayat recommendation unless direct 70%+ route
schemes.conditional_documents: Medical/intellectual-disability proof for income exemption; Age proof for 70+ rate; No-other-pension declaration if requested; Him Access/e-KYC documents if portal migration applies
schemes.application_mode: Offline prescribed-form application through Panchayat, Tehsil Welfare Officer or District Welfare Officer; Gram Sabha identifies eligible persons. ESOMSA Him Access/e-Kalyan now advertises login, family verification and document upload, so confirm migration for this pension.
schemes.application_steps: Obtain permanent disability certificate and residence, family, income and bank documents.; Submit form to Panchayat/Gram Sabha, TWO or DWO; 70%+ applicants may submit directly.; Gram Sabha/Panchayat verifies where required; TWO completes formalities and forwards to DWO.; After sanction, provide bank/PFMS details and retain pension order.; Provide life/continuation information and report changed income, family or other-pension status.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No fixed annual deadline found. Apply when eligible; continuation is subject to pension/life verification and updated ESOMSA requirements.
schemes.tracking_grievance: TWO/DWO; ESOMSA pension-form queries list 0177-3525101 and 0177-3525102. Use Him Access/e-Kalyan status if migrated and Mukhya Mantri Sewa Sankalp 1100 for unresolved grievances.

schemes.scheme_name: Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) — employment card and work demand
schemes.jurisdiction: India; Gram Panchayat, Programme Officer and State/UT VB-G RAM G administration
schemes.administering_body: Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development; implemented through State/UT schemes, Gram Panchayats and Programme Officers under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025
schemes.benefit_summary: From 1 July 2026, VB-G RAM G replaced MGNREGA and guarantees 125 days of unskilled wage employment in a financial year to each eligible rural household whose adult members volunteer for such work. Existing e-KYC-verified MGNREGA job cards remain valid during the transition until new Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards are issued. Work-demand, unemployment-allowance and wage-payment rights continue under the new Act and notified State/UT scheme.
schemes.eligibility_text: A rural household whose adult members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work may register through the Gram Panchayat. Every adult member seeking work should be recorded on the household employment card. Existing e-KYC-verified MGNREGA job cards remain valid during transition; a worker must not be denied employment merely because e-KYC is pending, according to the official commencement guidance.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: State/UT rules now control the exact registration form, employment-card replacement timetable, notified wage, permissible works, peak agricultural-season pause and unemployment-allowance workflow. The household must still make and retain evidence of a dated work demand; a card alone is not an automatic allocation of all 125 days.
schemes.exclusions_text: This is a rural, household-based unskilled-work guarantee, not an urban employment programme. A person outside an eligible rural household, a request outside the notified work-demand process, duplicate or false registration, or work outside the State/UT scheme may be rejected. State rules govern verification and remedies.
schemes.documents_required: Household member names, ages and address/residence details; photographs of adult members; a job-card application (prescribed form or plain paper). Provide bank or post-office account details for wage payment and a mobile number where available. Aadhaar/e-KYC may be requested for payment authentication but the job-card application should not be blocked solely for lack of Aadhaar.
schemes.conditional_documents: Residence proof, ration card, voter ID or other locally accepted identity/address evidence may be requested by the Gram Panchayat; bank/post-office passbook and Aadhaar/e-KYC support the payment workflow. Carry the existing MGNREGA job card during transition and ask for a dated receipt for registration, card replacement and every work demand.
schemes.application_mode: Assisted/offline at the Gram Panchayat or Programme Officer under the notified State/UT VB-G RAM G scheme; the national MIS remains available for records and monitoring. Registration and work demand remain local even where a State offers an online channel.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Take the existing MGNREGA job card, if any, to the Gram Panchayat and confirm its transition status. 2) Register missing adult household members or request the new Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Card under the State/UT scheme. 3) Submit a written or notified digital demand for work and retain the dated receipt. 4) Check allocation, muster roll and wage-payment records in the local office/MIS. 5) If work, unemployment allowance or wages are delayed, complain to the Programme Officer/District Programme Coordinator and use the notified grievance/Ombudsperson route.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Registration and recurring work demand are available through the year under the State/UT scheme. The annual statutory guarantee is now 125 days per eligible rural household. Keep household, employment-card, e-KYC and bank details current.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Use the national/state MIS for employment-card, demand, muster-roll and wage status where records are published. Escalate to the Gram Panchayat, Programme Officer, District Programme Coordinator, State grievance authority and notified Ombudsperson/social-audit mechanism.
schemes.source_authority: India Code and Ministry of Rural Development/PIB commencement guidance for the VB-G RAM G Act; State/UT notification and local records control an individual case
schemes.next_review_action: For Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Chandigarh, capture the notified State/UT VB-G RAM G scheme, current employment-card form, wage, work-demand receipt, payment instructions and Ombudsperson contact.

schemes.scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana 2.0 (PMMVY 2.0)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; Ministry of Women and Child Development implemented through States/UTs, Anganwadi Workers and ASHA/health functionaries
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of Women and Child Development; State/UT Women and Child Development departments and field functionaries
schemes.benefit_summary: For an eligible first child, ₹5,000 in two instalments subject to pregnancy registration/ANC and childbirth/early-immunisation conditions; JSY may provide a separate maternity benefit where applicable. For a second child, ₹6,000 in one instalment where the child is a girl, subject to the PMMVY 2.0 conditions and the birth-date/registration rules.
schemes.eligibility_text: A pregnant or lactating woman must generally be 18 years 7 months to below 55 years at childbirth and belong to at least one listed vulnerability/category: family income below ₹8 lakh, MGNREGA job-card holder, PM-KISAN woman farmer, e-Shram card holder, PM-JAY beneficiary, BPL ration-card holder, Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe, 40% or more disability, pregnant/lactating AWW/AWH/ASHA, NFSA ration-card holder, or another category specified in the current PMMVY FAQ. First-child benefit applies to the first living child; second-child benefit is for a girl child born on or after 1 April 2022 as stated in the current official FAQ.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The current FAQ and State implementation must be checked for the pregnancy/childbirth cut-off, first-living-child test, category proof accepted in a particular State and whether a State is implementing PMMVY or its own maternity scheme. The official brief has historically noted Odisha and Telangana as non-implementing; verify before presenting the route in those States.
schemes.exclusions_text: Not available for a pregnancy/childbirth that does not satisfy the age, first-child/second-girl, category-proof or registration/ANC/immunisation conditions. Duplicate claims, false category claims, missing Aadhaar-linked payment details and applications outside the 270-day post-childbirth window can be rejected. State maternity schemes may replace or affect the route.
schemes.documents_required: Beneficiary Aadhaar; Aadhaar-mapped bank or post-office account; mobile number; MCP/RCHI card; LMP and ANC details; childbirth registration/birth certificate; child's immunisation details; and one accepted eligibility-category proof such as income certificate, MGNREGA job card, PM-KISAN record, e-Shram card, PM-JAY record, BPL/NFSA ration card, disability certificate, SC/ST certificate or AWW/AWH/ASHA employment proof.
schemes.conditional_documents: Husband's Aadhaar is not mandatory according to the official FAQ. For a second-girl claim, girl-child birth details and proof of the relevant pregnancy/childbirth are required. A field functionary may request additional bank, address, category or immunisation evidence where the portal cannot validate it.
schemes.application_mode: Self-registration on the PMMVY portal or assisted digital application through an Anganwadi Worker/ASHA/approved health functionary. It is an open claim route for eligible women, subject to State implementation and field verification.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm State implementation and identify an AWW/ASHA or use https://pmmvy.wcd.gov.in. 2) Prepare Aadhaar, Aadhaar-linked account, mobile, MCP/RCHI record and one category proof. 3) Register pregnancy and upload/enter LMP and ANC information. 4) After delivery, record childbirth and submit birth/immunisation evidence. 5) For a second girl, select the second-child route and submit the girl-child records. 6) Check instalment status on the portal or through the field functionary; correct rejected data before the deadline.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No annual renewal. The official FAQ says the beneficiary may apply within 270 days of childbirth; pregnancy registration, ANC, childbirth registration and early immunisation milestones also have timing conditions. A second-girl claim must satisfy the current birth-date and 270-day rules.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track on the PMMVY portal through the beneficiary/application record or ask the AWW/ASHA. Escalate to the Child Development Project Officer, District Programme Officer and State/UT Women and Child Development department; use the official PMMVY portal grievance/contact route.
schemes.source_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development/official PMMVY FAQ and scheme page; State WCD implementation records control eligibility processing

schemes.scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; loans sanctioned by participating banks, RRBs, small finance banks, NBFCs and MFIs
schemes.administering_body: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance; MUDRA ecosystem and participating Member Lending Institutions
schemes.benefit_summary: Collateral-free institutional credit for income-generating micro enterprises, including non-farm businesses and specified allied agricultural activities such as poultry, dairy and beekeeping. Categories are Shishu up to ₹50,000; Kishore above ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh; Tarun above ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh; and Tarun Plus above ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh for an entrepreneur who has successfully repaid a prior Tarun loan, effective 24 October 2024. The lender decides pricing, tenure and sanction.
schemes.eligibility_text: Individuals and eligible micro-enterprise forms such as proprietorships, partnerships, private limited companies and other entities may apply through a participating lender for a viable income-generating activity. The borrower must satisfy the lender's KYC, credit, business-viability and repayment assessment. PMMY is a credit facility, not an automatic grant or entitlement.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: There is no single national minimum income, credit-score, margin or project-cost test in the public scheme summary; each lender applies its credit policy, sector exclusions, repayment capacity and required contribution. Tarun Plus requires successful repayment of a previous Tarun loan. Confirm whether a proposed activity is eligible and which lender product applies.
schemes.exclusions_text: Not a cash grant. A lender may decline an application for inadequate repayment capacity, deficient KYC, an ineligible/non-income-generating activity, adverse credit history, fraud or missing project information. Collateral is not required under PMMY, but lenders can require normal documentation, margin or guarantees as permitted by their product/risk policy.
schemes.documents_required: Applicant identity and address proof, recent photograph/signature, bank account details, enterprise identity/address proof, business constitution/registration where applicable, quotation or project report, projected sales/cash flow, licences/permits and tax/financial records where the lender asks for them. Exact documents vary by loan size and lender.
schemes.conditional_documents: SC/ST/OBC/minority or women-entrepreneur evidence may be requested for reporting or targeted products; GST/Udyam registration, shop/establishment licence, rent/ownership proof, prior loan closure statement and supplier quotations are conditional on the activity and lender. Tarun Plus requires proof of successful prior Tarun repayment.
schemes.application_mode: Open lender application online through JanSamarth/MUDRA channel or offline at a participating bank, RRB, SFB, NBFC or MFI branch. Final sanction is by the Member Lending Institution, not by a central portal.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Define the business, loan amount/category and use of funds. 2) Prepare KYC, bank details, business proof and a concise project/cash-flow plan. 3) Apply through https://www.jansamarth.in or https://www.mudra.org.in, or visit a participating lender. 4) Complete lender KYC, appraisal and any site/credit checks. 5) Review the sanction letter, interest, fees, repayment schedule and security terms before accepting. 6) Track disbursement and preserve repayment/closure records; a successful Tarun repayment is relevant for Tarun Plus.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No national application deadline or annual renewal. Apply when finance is needed; loan renewal/top-up is lender-specific and subject to repayment performance and fresh appraisal.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track with the selected bank/NBFC/MFI branch and its grievance officer; use JanSamarth status where the application was initiated there. Escalate unresolved service complaints through the lender's nodal officer and the applicable RBI/Ombudsman route; MUDRA does not itself sanction each loan.

schemes.next_review_action: For the pilot region, map participating lenders and their current PMMY checklist, JanSamarth workflow, fees, interest/tenure and grievance contacts.

application_route.deadline_or_renewal: No national application deadline or annual renewal. Apply when finance is needed; loan renewal/top-up is lender-specific and subject to repayment performance and fresh appraisal.
application_route.tracking_or_grievance: Track with the selected bank/NBFC/MFI branch and its grievance officer; use JanSamarth status where the application was initiated there. Escalate unresolved service complaints through the lender's nodal officer and the applicable RBI/Ombudsman route; MUDRA does not itself sanction each loan.

schemes.scheme_name: PM Vishwakarma
schemes.jurisdiction: India; Central Sector Scheme with verification by Gram Panchayat/Urban Local Body and delivery through CSCs, training institutions and lenders
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, with partner ministries/agencies including SIDBI and participating lenders
schemes.benefit_summary: Support for eligible traditional artisans and craftspeople in 18 listed trades: recognition through PM Vishwakarma certificate and ID card, basic and advanced skill training, toolkit incentive up to ₹15,000, training stipend reported at ₹500 per day, digital-transaction incentive, marketing support and collateral-free concessional loans in stages (first loan ₹1 lakh and second loan ₹2 lakh, at the notified interest rate, commonly 5%).
schemes.eligibility_text: An artisan/craftsperson aged 18 or above who is self-employed and engaged in one of the 18 notified traditional trades may apply through a CSC/portal. Trades include carpenter, boat maker, armourer, blacksmith, hammer/tool-kit maker, locksmith, goldsmith, potter, sculptor/stone carver/stone breaker, cobbler/shoesmith/footwear artisan, mason, basket/mat/broom/coir weaver, doll/toy maker, barber, garland maker, washerman, tailor and fishing-net maker. Local-body verification and skill/trade verification are part of onboarding.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The public scheme summaries do not expose every current exclusion and family/previous-benefit rule in one place. Confirm the live portal guideline for one beneficiary per family, recent receipt of similar credit/subsidy, trade evidence, state/ULB verification, training attendance and loan-stage conditions before promising eligibility.
schemes.exclusions_text: Only the 18 notified trades and qualifying self-employment are in scope. Applicants below 18, non-artisan applicants, duplicate/fraudulent profiles, persons failing Gram Panchayat/ULB or skill verification, and applicants barred by current scheme rules or unresolved prior benefits can be rejected. Loan release additionally depends on lender appraisal and completion of required training/first-stage conditions.
schemes.documents_required: Aadhaar and mobile number for registration/e-KYC; bank account details; address and family details; occupation/trade information; photograph and other identity data requested by the portal/CSC. Keep any local-body/trade proof, Udyam or business evidence and training/verification record available.
schemes.conditional_documents: CSC/ULB may request ration card, residence proof, caste/category or disability evidence, trade/work photographs, certificate from a local authority, prior-loan details or other evidence where Aadhaar and database checks do not establish the facts. Lenders require their normal KYC and loan documents.
schemes.application_mode: Assisted application at a Common Service Centre and on https://pmvishwakarma.gov.in; verification by Gram Panchayat/ULB and a three-stage process (local verification, district/state review and screening) precedes certificate/training and benefits. It is an open registration route for qualifying artisans, not an automatic grant.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Visit a CSC or the official portal and select the correct one of the 18 trades. 2) Complete Aadhaar/mobile e-KYC and bank details. 3) Submit for Gram Panchayat/ULB verification and subsequent review. 4) On approval, receive the certificate/ID, complete basic/advanced training and claim toolkit support. 5) Use the digital incentive/marketing channels as applicable. 6) Apply for the first and later loan through the linked lender only after meeting the current training/repayment conditions.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: The scheme was approved for five years from FY 2023-24 through FY 2027-28. Registration is subject to the live portal/implementation window; certificate does not require annual renewal, but training, digital-incentive and staged-loan conditions must be met when claimed.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track registration and verification with the CSC/PM Vishwakarma portal and the local Gram Panchayat/ULB. For loan issues, contact the participating lender; for scheme/service issues, use the portal/CSC escalation and MSME/State nodal channels.
schemes.source_authority: MSME Ministry official scheme materials and PM Vishwakarma portal; local verification and lender records control individual outcomes
schemes.next_review_action: Capture the current PM Vishwakarma portal FAQ/operational guideline, registration status and CSC checklist; verify the 18-trade list and family/prior-benefit restrictions before pilot use.

schemes.scheme_name: e-Shram — National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; registration gateway with Central/State linked welfare schemes
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of Labour and Employment; e-Shram/NDUW portal with CSC/State Seva Kendra assisted registration
schemes.benefit_summary: Free registration creates a permanent Universal Account Number (UAN) and an e-Shram card in the national database of unorganised workers. Registration itself does not automatically pay a cash benefit; linked social-security, employment and welfare schemes retain their own eligibility, application and sanction rules.
schemes.eligibility_text: An unorganised worker aged 16–59, including construction, migrant, gig/platform, street-vendor, domestic, agriculture and similar workers, may register. The worker should not be an income-tax payer and should not be covered as an EPFO/ESIC member or a government-funded NPS beneficiary under the current FAQ. Aadhaar and an Aadhaar-linked mobile are the normal self-registration route.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The portal is a database/gateway rather than a single benefit scheme. The definition of unorganised worker, tax/EPFO/ESIC/NPS status and any linked scheme's eligibility must be assessed separately. A worker may need to update occupation, bank and migration details for a downstream scheme.
schemes.exclusions_text: Current FAQ exclusions include income-tax payers and workers already covered by EPFO, ESIC or government-funded NPS; age outside 16–59 is outside the registration rule. Registration can fail for invalid Aadhaar/mobile, duplicate UAN or inaccurate information. It is not proof of entitlement to every social-security scheme.
schemes.documents_required: Aadhaar number and Aadhaar-linked mobile number; bank account/IFSC details are strongly recommended and may be required for profile/benefit linkage. If the mobile is not Aadhaar-linked, visit a CSC/SSK for biometric registration.
schemes.conditional_documents: CSC/SSK may seek biometric authentication and identity/profile corrections. Downstream welfare schemes can require occupation, income, domicile, ration card, disability, age, bank or other scheme-specific documents.
schemes.application_mode: Open, free self-registration on the e-Shram portal or assisted biometric registration at a CSC/State Seva Kendra. UAN card has no expiry and no annual renewal, but profile details should be updated when they change.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Visit https://eshram.gov.in and choose registration/update. 2) Authenticate Aadhaar and mobile; if mobile is not linked, use a CSC/SSK. 3) Enter occupation, address, bank and other profile data accurately. 4) Download/save the UAN/e-Shram card. 5) Update profile after migration, occupation, mobile or bank changes. 6) Use the linked-schemes page only as a discovery channel and apply separately under each scheme.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No last date; registration is available 24x7. UAN/e-Shram card does not expire and has no annual renewal requirement. Updates are ongoing and should be made when data changes.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Use the e-Shram portal's update/status functions, call 14434 or 1800-889-6811 (official FAQ helpdesk hours), file a grievance at https://gms.eshram.gov.in, or seek CSC assistance. For a linked benefit, track with that scheme's administering department rather than e-Shram.
schemes.source_authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment official e-Shram objectives/FAQ/portal; linked scheme authorities control actual benefits
schemes.next_review_action: Keep the record as a gateway and map each target State's linked welfare schemes, data-sharing consent and benefit-specific application requirements.

schemes.scheme_name: National Food Security Act (NFSA) ration-card entitlement and One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; ration-card beneficiary identification and issue by States/UTs; foodgrain allocation/ONORC portability coordinated by Department of Food and Public Distribution
schemes.administering_body: Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; State/UT Food and Civil Supplies departments issue cards and identify beneficiaries
schemes.benefit_summary: NFSA entitlement is up to 5 kg foodgrains per person per month for Priority Households (PHH) and 35 kg per household per month for Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY), currently distributed free under the notified PMGKAY continuation. ONORC lets an existing NFSA beneficiary lift entitled foodgrains from any ePoS fair-price shop in the country using the same ration card/Aadhaar after biometric or OTP authentication.
schemes.eligibility_text: NFSA coverage is list/entitlement based: States/UTs identify eligible rural households up to 75% and urban households up to 50% using their own criteria within the national coverage framework, issue ration cards and maintain the beneficiary database. An existing valid NFSA PHH/AAY card is the prerequisite for ONORC portability. A new ration card is a State/UT application, not a single central application.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: State inclusion criteria, income/occupation/residence tests, documents, family-member addition/deletion, duplicate-card handling and waiting lists differ. A migrant can use ONORC only if the home State card is active and the family/member is seeded and authenticated; portability does not itself create a new entitlement or add a person to the NFSA list.
schemes.exclusions_text: Persons/households not selected under the relevant State/UT NFSA criteria, duplicate/inactive/cancelled cards, unverified family members, failed biometric/OTP authentication or non-NFSA cards cannot claim ONORC NFSA portability. Commodity quantity, shops, authentication fallback and local exclusions follow State/TPDS and current central orders.
schemes.documents_required: For a new or corrected ration-card application, State/UT forms commonly require Aadhaar/identity of members, address/residence proof, family details, photographs, mobile number and bank/income/category evidence where the State asks. For ONORC use, carry the valid ration-card number and Aadhaar/OTP-enabled mobile; biometrics are taken at the ePoS shop.
schemes.conditional_documents: Birth/death/marriage certificates for member changes, migration/residence proof, surrender/deletion certificate for a previous card, disability/SC/ST/category or income proof and landlord/utility documents may be required by the State. Authentication fallback or e-KYC may require additional identity verification.
schemes.application_mode: State/UT Food and Civil Supplies portal, district office, ration-card service centre or fair-price-shop/CSC channel for a new card or correction. ONORC is not a new central benefit application: an existing NFSA cardholder uses any participating ePoS fair-price shop or the Mera Ration app.
schemes.application_steps: 1) For a new card, apply to the State/UT Food and Civil Supplies authority using its current form and documents. 2) Wait for household/member verification and inclusion in the State NFSA/TPDS list. 3) Complete Aadhaar seeding/e-KYC where the State requires it. 4) For portability, visit an ePoS FPS in the destination State, present the card/Aadhaar and authenticate by biometric or OTP. 5) Check entitlement and transaction history in the Mera Ration app/NFSA portal. 6) If denied, record the FPS/ePoS transaction and use the State grievance officer/DGRO or Food Commission.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No national ONORC application deadline or annual renewal. A ration card remains subject to State verification and household changes; update/delete/add members promptly. Foodgrain quantities and free-distribution continuation follow current central orders and can change.
schemes.tracking_grievance: NFSA portal supports grievance registration and status tracking; use the State Food/Civil Supplies portal, FPS dealer, District Grievance Redressal Officer, State Food Commission and vigilance/social-audit channels. Mera Ration shows entitlement, transactions, Aadhaar seeding and portability where data is available.
schemes.source_authority: DFPD and NFSA official pages/orders; State/UT Food and Civil Supplies beneficiary lists and ration-card records control individual eligibility
schemes.next_review_action: For Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Chandigarh, add current ration-card application URLs, State inclusion criteria, helplines, e-KYC/biometric fallback and Mera Ration availability before deployment.

schemes.scheme_name: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students (Punjab)
schemes.jurisdiction: Punjab; Punjab-domiciled SC students studying after matriculation, including outside-Punjab institutions where accepted
schemes.administering_body: Department of Social Justice, Empowerment and Minorities, Government of Punjab; institution verification authority; National Scholarship Portal for the 2026-27 route
schemes.benefit_summary: Fee support and scholarship assistance for eligible Punjab SC students after matriculation. Current 2026-27 Panjab University guidance says normal-course Punjab SC students with annual family income up to Rs 2.50 lakh are not charged tuition/non-refundable fees (refundable security remains); self-financing students pay 25% of first and second semester fees pending reimbursement. Exact maintenance/fee rates vary by course/group under the current PMS guidelines.
schemes.eligibility_text: Student belongs to the Scheduled Caste category recognised for Punjab; Punjab state domicile/residence; post-matric/post-secondary course in a recognised institution; annual family/parent-guardian income up to Rs 2.50 lakh according to current 2026-27 guidance; must satisfy the live PMS course, institution, attendance, renewal and de-duplication rules. The current PU guidance requires an undertaking that the student has not taken another course or another PMS claim for the same session/course.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm current Punjab-wide course/group rates, attendance rule, exact domicile certificate requirement, fresh versus renewal treatment, whether all institutions use NSP or Punjab Dr Ambedkar portal for 2026-27, and whether the Rs 2.50 lakh ceiling is unchanged in the final Punjab circular.
schemes.exclusions_text: Other scholarship/duplicate PMS claim for the same course/session; non-SC or non-Punjab student; family income above the applicable ceiling; unrecognised course/institution; incomplete, mismatched or late application; failure of institutional verification. The live 2026 circular controls any further exclusions.
schemes.documents_required: SC caste certificate in the student's name; current parent/guardian income certificate; Punjab residence/domicile certificate; Aadhaar of student and parent/guardian; previous/last examination marksheet or DMC; current admission/course/institution details; bank account/passbook for DBT; applicant undertaking/affidavit; photograph where portal asks.
schemes.conditional_documents: Freeship card for applicable renewal/eligible students; fee receipt/fee structure for self-financing courses; disability/hostel/other category evidence if a course-group rate requires it; institution-specific hard-copy checklist.
schemes.application_mode: Online. Current 2026-27 PU guidance directs Punjab SC students to National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in); Punjab's official service page also links the Punjab Dr Ambedkar Scholarship Portal (scholarships.punjab.gov.in). Institution verifies and forwards the application; some institutions require a printed form/hard copies.
schemes.application_steps: Generate NSP One-Time Registration and complete Aadhaar face authentication where NSP requires it; select the correct PMS-SC scheme and institution; enter demographic, caste, income, course and bank data; upload clear documents; accept undertaking and final-submit; download/print the application; give printout/documents to the institution if instructed; monitor institute/district/state verification and DBT status.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Academic-session deadlines are announced by NSP/Punjab and may be extended. The reviewed official 2026 notices confirm the 2026-27 cycle but not a single final Punjab deadline. Renewal/fresh status must follow the session notice; do not assume a year-round window.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track on NSP after final submission and through the institution's scholarship/nodal office. Punjab portal/Connect and the Department of Social Justice may handle state queries; institution-level correction is usually required before state/central verification. Current scheme-specific Punjab grievance number was not exposed.

schemes.next_review_action: Obtain the Punjab Department's final 2026-27 PMS-SC circular and verify the live application portal, exact date, course-group rates, attendance and domicile rules.

schemes.scheme_name: Bebe Nanki Ladli Beti Kalyan Scheme
schemes.administering_body: Department of Social Security and Development of Women & Children, Government of Punjab; District Programme Officer (DPO)/Child Development Project Officer
schemes.benefit_summary: Official Punjab welfare information describes staged financial assistance totalling Rs 61,000 to the guardian of an eligible girl up to age 18. The reviewed official page/service listing does not publish a current instalment table or a recent sanction order, so the stage-wise amount should be confirmed with the DPO.
schemes.eligibility_text: Girl born on or after 1 January 2011; parents are permanent Punjab residents; abandoned girl found on/after that date and living in a Punjab orphanage/Children's Home is also included; number of girls born before the cut-off is not counted; newly born boys are not eligible; annual family income must be below Rs 30,000 and proof is stated as a Blue Card issued by Punjab Food and Supplies; benefits stop from the date the girl drops out of school.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm whether the 1 January 2011 cut-off, Rs 30,000 income/Blue Card rule, school-continuation rule and Rs 61,000 total remain current for new applications in 2026, and whether any birth-date transition or instalment backlog rule applies.
schemes.exclusions_text: Newly born boys; family income at/above the published ceiling or no Blue Card/income proof; girl outside the birth-date/residence/orphanage conditions; and dropout from school. Current detailed exclusions and duplicate-benefit rules are not published on the accessible department page.
schemes.documents_required: Guardian address/residence proof; guardian Aadhaar; girl's birth certificate; income proof; Blue Card; bank account details. Carry girl/guardian identity and school-continuation proof if requested by DPO.
schemes.conditional_documents: Orphanage/Children's Home custody or institutional certificate for abandoned girls; school enrolment/attendance/continuation certificate for instalment release; caste/family records only if the DPO's current form requests them.

schemes.administering_body: Government of Punjab; Department of Cooperation / District Central Cooperative Banks and Primary Agricultural Cooperative Societies (PACS), with Agriculture and Finance departments involved
schemes.benefit_summary: Historical Punjab Government records describe a Rs 520 crore waiver for about 2.85 lakh farm labourers and landless farmers who were members of PACS. schemes.eligibility_text: The historical implementation targeted farm labourers and landless farming members of Primary Agricultural Cooperative Societies in Punjab. Public implementation reporting describes consumption loans advanced by District Central Cooperative Banks through PACS, with the waiver tied to historical loan principal/cut-off and interest periods. Exact live account, membership, cut-off and category verification must be obtained from the relevant PACS/DCCB.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm whether all sanctioned phases are closed, whether any residual/rejected claims remain open, exact loan cut-off dates, maximum waiver per member, treatment of non-PACS/commercial loans, landless definition, deceased/successor claims and whether a new government has renewed or replaced the scheme.
schemes.exclusions_text: Historical scope excludes ordinary non-PACS/non-eligible loan products and likely excludes loans outside the notified cut-off, duplicate claims or persons not verified as PACS farm-labour/landless members. These are not a current published exclusion list.
schemes.documents_required: No current official checklist found. For a historical claim enquiry, carry Aadhaar/identity, Punjab residence, PACS membership/passbook or loan account number, loan statement, landless/farm-labour evidence if held, bank details and any earlier waiver acknowledgement.
schemes.conditional_documents: Death/legal-heir documents for successor claims; caste/occupation or land-record evidence if the DCCB asks; PACS resolution/loan ledger and bank certificate are likely required for reconciliation.

schemes.scheme_name: National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) – Punjab implementation
schemes.jurisdiction: Punjab (NSAP centrally sponsored scheme implemented by Punjab Social Security and Women & Child Development Department)
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of Rural Development under NSAP; Department of Social Security and Women & Child Development, Government of Punjab; District Social Security Officer
schemes.benefit_summary: One-time Rs 20,000 assistance to an eligible BPL bereaved household on death of the primary breadwinner. The current central NSAP description confirms Rs 20,000 and demand-based state processing. Punjab's official form is still marked last revised August 2017 and district guidance says apply within one year, so current Punjab processing requirements require confirmation.
schemes.eligibility_text: BPL household; death of the primary/main earning member; the Punjab form states the main earning member's age at death is 18-64, while current national/ Punjab district references commonly state 18-59. Punjab district guidance says the surviving widow/household may claim and application should be made within one year from death. The applicant must establish the household/BPL and deceased breadwinner relationship.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Resolve the conflicting age rule (Punjab form 18-64 versus current NSAP/district 18-59), whether the one-year filing rule is current statewide, whether BPL is now verified through SECC/food-supply data, and whether survivor/head-of-household wording has changed.
schemes.exclusions_text: Non-BPL household; death not of the primary breadwinner; age outside the notified band; claim beyond the current deadline; duplicate NFBS claim; missing death/BPL/relationship proof. Exact current exclusion/capacity rules follow NSAP and Punjab circulars.
schemes.documents_required: Death certificate; self-declaration; BPL card/number and family ID/member ID where available; Aadhaar/enrolment and Voter ID of applicant/deceased where available; applicant address/contact and bank/payment details; relationship proof if not apparent from family record.
schemes.conditional_documents: Post-mortem/FIR or cause-of-death evidence if the verifier requests it; legal-heir/survivor certificate; residence or family register; bank account/mandate for current DBT route. The official form specifically requires scanned death certificate and self-declaration.
schemes.application_mode: Sewa Kendra or other district Social Security intake; the official form also lists by-post submission. Punjab forms page lists NFBS under Social Security and Women & Child Development. Confirm whether Connect/eServices online submission is enabled in the applicant's district.
schemes.application_steps: Collect death, BPL/family and identity/relationship documents; obtain the NFBS form from the District Social Security Officer/Sewa Kendra; submit within the currently confirmed period; receive acknowledgement; district verifies BPL, breadwinner age and death; track sanction/payment and retain the certificate/payment record.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: One-time assistance; no renewal. Ludhiana district guidance says apply within one year of death, but the current statewide deadline must be confirmed. Punjab RTS material has historically listed 30-day disposal for sanction.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track through the District Social Security Officer/Sewa Kendra acknowledgement and Punjab eServices/Connect if the district accepts online filing; escalate under Punjab RTS to the District Social Security Officer and Additional Deputy Commissioner/Deputy Commissioner. National funds are released against state proposals and caps.

schemes.scheme_name: UT Chandigarh Widow / Destitute Pension
schemes.administering_body: Department of Social Welfare, Women and Child Development, Chandigarh Administration
schemes.benefit_summary: Current parliamentary information states Rs 1,000 per month from the Chandigarh Social Welfare widow pension scheme. A central NSAP top-up table separately shows Rs 300 central plus Rs 1,000 UT top-up (total Rs 1,300) for the NWPS component; applicants must confirm which layer/card they receive.
schemes.eligibility_text: Widow or destitute woman resident of Chandigarh, with three years' residence proof and income within the current social-welfare ceiling. The official ServiceOnline record requires Aadhaar, 3-year residence proof, bank passbook, age proof, and husband's death certificate for widow; for destitute cases it accepts an untraceability certificate or 100% disability certificate. Older official MHA reporting states annual income from all sources up to Rs 1.50 lakh, but current age/income rules are not fully exposed.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm minimum/maximum age, whether the Rs 1.50 lakh ceiling remains current, whether separated/deserted women qualify, the distinction between UT widow pension and NSAP widow pension, and whether current payment is Rs 1,000 or Rs 1,300 for the applicant's category.
schemes.exclusions_text: Likely no Chandigarh residence/three-year proof, income above current ceiling, no widow/destitution evidence, duplicate pension or unverified bank/identity data. Current ServiceOnline page does not publish a complete exclusion list.
schemes.documents_required: Aadhaar; residential proof of three years (ration/voter/telephone/electricity bill, passport or prescribed residence certificate); bank passbook; age proof or age-assessment certificate from listed government hospital/dispensary; husband's death certificate for widow applicants.
schemes.conditional_documents: Untraceability certificate or 100% disability certificate for destitute route; domicile/resident certificate of ex-servicemen/widows from Tehsildar/SDM; relationship/legal-heir or other documents if the verifier requests them.
schemes.application_mode: Online via Chandigarh ServiceOnline service ID 16400001; assisted submission/e-Sampark or Social Welfare office is also used for social-welfare applications and verification.
schemes.application_steps: Register/login on ServiceOnline and select UT Chandigarh Widow Pension; upload Aadhaar, 3-year residence, age, bank and death/destitution evidence; submit and keep acknowledgement; attend Social Welfare/e-Sampark verification; resolve queries; track sanction/payment and distinguish UT-only versus NSAP component.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: ServiceOnline currently shows no fixed delivery period (NA), and no application closing date was found. Pension is recurring; annual/life verification and renewal rules need confirmation.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Use ServiceOnline acknowledgement/status where available; follow up with Department of Social Welfare/e-Sampark. Chandigarh RTS escalation applies if a notified service deadline is missed, but the reviewed ServiceOnline entry does not state a deadline or grievance URL.

schemes.scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; enrollment and premium collection through participating banks/post offices with partner general insurers
schemes.administering_body: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance; participating banks/post offices and approved general insurance companies
schemes.benefit_summary: One-year renewable personal accident cover: ₹2 lakh for accidental death or total permanent disability and ₹1 lakh for specified partial permanent disability. Current annual premium is ₹20 per member, collected by one-time auto-debit.
schemes.eligibility_text: An individual (single or joint) savings-bank or post-office account holder aged 18 through 70 years in a participating institution may opt in, give consent for auto-debit and satisfy the account/KYC requirements. A person with multiple accounts may enroll through only one account. NRI account holders with an eligible Indian bank account may join subject to scheme terms.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The enrolling bank/post office and its insurer must be participating and the account must remain operative with sufficient balance on the premium debit date. Exact accident definitions, disability certification and claim documents are governed by the current rules/policy and insurer.
schemes.exclusions_text: No cover for ordinary illness/non-accidental death, risks outside the policy definition or claims not supported by the prescribed accident/disability evidence. Cover terminates on attaining age 70, account closure, insufficient balance, duplicate enrollment through multiple accounts or withdrawal; only one cover is valid even if premium is debited more than once.
schemes.documents_required: Bank/post-office account and KYC details, Aadhaar as primary KYC for the account where available, mobile number and nominee/appointee details; signed consent-cum-declaration/auto-debit authorization. For a claim, death certificate or prescribed accident/disability proof, claimant identity/KYC, bank details and the enrollment/consent record.
schemes.conditional_documents: Age/date-of-birth proof if not established in KYC; legal-heir proof where there is no nomination; medical/disability certificate, FIR/post-mortem/panchanama or hospital records where required by the claim form and insurer.
schemes.application_mode: Assisted or digital opt-in through a participating bank branch, internet/mobile banking, BC or post office; the bank/post office sends consent to the partner insurer. No central individual entitlement portal replaces the account-level enrollment.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm age and an eligible savings account. 2) Ask the bank/post office for PMSBY or use its digital enrollment option. 3) Submit consent-cum-declaration, nominee and auto-debit authorization. 4) Ensure ₹20 is available on the notified annual debit date and retain acknowledgement/certificate. 5) For a claim, notify the bank/post office promptly and submit the official PMSBY claim form and prescribed evidence to the bank/insurer.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Cover normally runs 1 June–31 May and renews annually by auto-debit; late enrollment may be allowed subject to current rules and premium. No permanent one-time registration: keep consent and balance active each renewal.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Check enrollment/debit and certificate with the bank/post office; use the Jansuraksha portal information/forms at https://jansuraksha.gov.in/. Claim complaints go first to the bank/insurer grievance officer, then the insurer/IRDAI grievance route or CPGRAMS as appropriate.
schemes.source_authority: Department of Financial Services rules/FAQ and India Post official scheme page; participating bank/insurer records control enrollment and claims
schemes.next_review_action: Confirm the pilot bank/post office's current digital enrollment path, annual debit date, partner insurer and claim form/turnaround before user deployment.

schemes.scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; enrollment and premium collection through participating banks/post offices with LIC or other approved life insurers
schemes.administering_body: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance; participating banks/post offices and LIC/approved life insurance companies
schemes.benefit_summary: One-year renewable term life cover of ₹2 lakh payable to the nominee on death due to any cause. Current annual premium is ₹436 per subscriber, normally collected by one-time auto-debit; first-time mid-year enrollment may use the official pro-rata premium schedule.
schemes.eligibility_text: An individual (single or joint) savings-bank or post-office account holder aged 18 through 50 years in a participating institution may join by giving prescribed consent and auto-debit authorization. Only one account can be used for a person. An NRI may join with an eligible Indian bank account subject to scheme terms.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The bank/post office must be participating and the account must remain active with sufficient balance for renewal. The insurer's current rules govern age calculation, first-time enrollment, lien period, nomination and proof of death. This is voluntary term insurance, not a government pension or maturity-value product.
schemes.exclusions_text: There is no maturity or surrender benefit. For a first-time enrollee, death from a cause other than accident during the first 30 days after enrollment is not admissible; accidental death is covered from risk commencement under the current DFS material. Cover stops on attaining age 55, account closure/insufficient balance, withdrawal or duplicate enrollment; only one cover is valid.
schemes.documents_required: Bank/post-office account and KYC details, Aadhaar as primary KYC for the account where available, mobile number, nominee/appointee details, signed consent-cum-declaration and auto-debit authorization. For claims: death certificate, claimant/nominee KYC and bank details, enrollment record and any prescribed cause-of-death/accident evidence.
schemes.conditional_documents: Age/date-of-birth proof where KYC is incomplete; legal-heir/succession proof where nomination is absent or disputed; guardian/appointee proof for a minor nominee and additional hospital, police or medical records where the insurer's claim form asks for them.
schemes.application_mode: Assisted or digital opt-in through a participating bank branch, internet/mobile banking, BC or post office. The account institution transmits the consent to LIC/partner insurer; there is no substitute central self-enrollment that guarantees a policy.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm age 18–50 and an eligible account. 2) Request PMJJBY enrollment from the bank/post office or use its digital journey. 3) Submit consent, nominee and auto-debit authorization. 4) Ensure the required premium is available and save the certificate/acknowledgement. 5) For a claim, the nominee/legal heir contacts the bank/post office and files the official PMJJBY claim form with death and identity/bank documents.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Risk period is generally 1 June–31 May and renews annually by auto-debit. New eligible entrants may join later with the applicable pro-rata premium; the 30-day non-accidental-death lien applies to first-time enrollment under current rules.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Confirm debit, policy/certificate and nominee with the bank/post office; scheme forms/rules are on https://jansuraksha.gov.in/. Escalate claim/service complaints to the bank/insurer grievance officer, insurer/IRDAI route or CPGRAMS as appropriate.

schemes.scheme_name: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; administered through PFRDA/NPS architecture and authorized banks/post offices
schemes.administering_body: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority under the National Pension System architecture; authorized banks and Department of Posts
schemes.benefit_summary: Voluntary, contribution-based pension. A subscriber joining at 18–40 selects a guaranteed minimum monthly pension of ₹1,000, ₹2,000, ₹3,000, ₹4,000 or ₹5,000 payable after age 60 for life; the same pension goes to the spouse after subscriber death, and accumulated pension wealth is returned to the nominee after both die. Contribution depends on entry age, pension slab and monthly/quarterly/half-yearly frequency.
schemes.eligibility_text: Any Indian citizen aged 18 to 40 with a savings bank or post-office savings account may join. From 1 October 2022, a person who is or has been an income-tax payer on the application date is not eligible to open a new APY account. Government/PSU employees and existing NPS subscribers may join if they satisfy the basic criteria.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The bank's onboarding/KYC and Aadhaar authentication workflow, contribution table and treatment of a subscriber becoming an income-tax payer after enrollment should be verified from current PFRDA rules. APY is not an open cash-benefit application; the applicant commits to recurring contributions until age 60.
schemes.exclusions_text: New applicants under 18 or over 40, and persons who are or have been income-tax payers on the application date, cannot open a new APY account. Missed contributions can attract overdue interest/charges and account action under rules; voluntary exit before 60 is restricted to permitted cases. APY is not a substitute for immediate pension.
schemes.documents_required: Savings bank/post-office account, APY registration form, KYC/identity and date-of-birth proof, mobile number, nominee and spouse details, selected pension slab/frequency and standing instruction/auto-debit authorization. Aadhaar may be provided and is required for authentication under current notified process.
schemes.conditional_documents: Spouse/nominee identity and age details, guardian details for a minor nominee, Aadhaar authentication, bank/post-office account opening documents and any correction/exit/death documents required by the institution.
schemes.application_mode: Assisted enrollment at the bank/post office holding the savings account, with some banks offering digital APY onboarding. The authorized institution opens the APY/NPS account and sets the standing instruction; no central direct cash-application portal exists.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm age 18–40, citizenship, non-taxpayer status at application and an eligible account. 2) Visit the account-holding bank/post office and request APY. 3) Choose the pension amount and contribution frequency using the current PFRDA table. 4) Submit KYC, spouse/nominee details and auto-debit authorization. 5) Retain PRAN/acknowledgement and monitor recurring debits. 6) Update bank, nominee or spouse information through the institution and use the permitted exit/death process if needed.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No national deadline; enrollment is open while the person is 18–40 and eligible. Contributions recur until age 60 and must be funded at the selected frequency; the account does not require an annual re-application but requires continuing contributions.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track contributions, PRAN and account changes through the APY service provider/bank/post office. Escalate first to the bank/post-office grievance officer, then PFRDA/CGMS or the applicable Ombudsman/CPGRAMS route.

schemes.next_review_action: Use the current PFRDA contribution calculator/table and verify the pilot bank/post office's APY onboarding, grievance and digital tracking path.

schemes.scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; notified crops/areas and seasonality are set by State/UT governments and insurers under national operational guidelines
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; State/UT agriculture departments, designated insurers, banks/PACS/CSCs and the National Crop Insurance Portal
schemes.benefit_summary: Crop insurance against notified non-preventable natural risks and specified prevented-sowing, localized and post-harvest losses for notified crops/areas. Farmer share is capped at 2% of sum insured for Kharif food/oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food/oilseed crops and 5% for annual commercial/horticultural crops; the applicable insurer pays eligible claims under the notified area/crop rules.
schemes.eligibility_text: A farmer with insurable interest in a notified crop and area, including owner cultivators and eligible sharecroppers/tenant farmers where State proof rules permit, may enroll. Participation is voluntary for loanee and non-loanee farmers under the revamped scheme, subject to crop/area notification, season cut-off and evidence of cultivation. Each State selects crops, insurance units and implementing insurers.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The current season's notified crops, villages/insurance units, sum insured, insurer, crop calendar, tenant/sharecropper proof and local cut-off date must be checked in the State notification; national indicative Kharif/Rabi dates are not a substitute. Some States route online applications through their own portal, and PMFBY excludes crops covered under a separate RWBCIS notification.
schemes.exclusions_text: A crop, farmer or area not notified for that season is not insurable under PMFBY. Intentional loss, excluded risks, false land/crop information, late premium/application, duplicate cover or lack of insurable interest can invalidate coverage. Claims depend on notified peril, area approach/CCE data and prescribed intimation windows; ordinary price loss or non-insured crops are not automatically covered.
schemes.documents_required: Farmer identity and mobile; land/tenancy or cultivation proof; crop, area and sowing details; bank account/passbook and IFSC; State farmer ID/land record or other prescribed ID; and premium payment. The official registration form asks name, age, address, farmer type/category, ID and bank details.
schemes.conditional_documents: Aadhaar/e-KYC, land record, lease/sharecropper certificate, KCC/loan account, sowing certificate, crop declaration, caste/category and bank verification vary by State, bank, CSC and insurer. Keep the proposal/acknowledgement and crop-insurance application number.
schemes.application_mode: Online through the National Crop Insurance Portal where enabled, or assisted through bank/PACS, CSC, insurance agent/BC or State agriculture office. This is a seasonal application; enrollment is open only for State-notified crop/area windows.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Check the State/season notification for crop, village, insurer, sum insured and cut-off. 2) Prepare cultivation/land proof, ID, bank details and crop declaration. 3) Apply via https://pmfby.gov.in/farmerRegistrationForm or the notified bank/PACS/CSC/State portal and pay the farmer premium. 4) Obtain acknowledgement/application number and verify policy status. 5) Report localized or post-harvest loss within the notified time (often 72 hours) through the insurer/portal/official channel. 6) Track claim assessment, CCE/area result and payment; appeal through the State/insurer grievance process.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Seasonal deadlines are State/crop/calendar specific. Official guidelines give indicative windows (often around 15 July for Kharif and 15 December for Rabi), but the State notification is final; no late application should be promised. Re-enroll and pay each season for the desired crop/area.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Use farmer login/application status at https://pmfby.gov.in/farmerApplicationLogin or https://pmfby.gov.in/farmerLogin, the insurer directory and State agriculture grievance channel. Contact the designated insurer, bank/CSC, District Level Monitoring Committee and State Level Coordination Committee; preserve acknowledgement and loss-intimation proof.

schemes.next_review_action: For each pilot State, ingest the current Kharif/Rabi notification, crop calendar, notified villages/crops, insurer, premium/sum insured, tenant-proof rules and loss-intimation contacts.

schemes.scheme_name: PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
schemes.jurisdiction: India; residential rooftop solar consumers connected to a State/UT DISCOM
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy; National Portal, State/UT DISCOMs, empanelled rooftop-solar vendors and financial institutions
schemes.benefit_summary: Central financial assistance for eligible residential grid-connected rooftop solar installed through the National Portal, with indicative CFA of ₹30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW and ₹18,000 per kW for the next 1 kW, capped at ₹78,000 for systems above 3 kW. Group housing/RWA common facilities have separate limits. The consumer pays the balance to the registered vendor; generation and bill savings depend on system/DISCOM/net-metering conditions.
schemes.eligibility_text: A residential electricity consumer with an eligible DISCOM connection can apply on the National Portal, select an empanelled vendor, obtain DISCOM approval, install the system, complete inspection/net-metering and submit bank details for CFA. CFA is for eligible residential rooftop systems meeting current technical, vendor, metering and portal conditions; commercial/industrial connections are not the residential CFA route.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: State/DISCOM eligibility, sanctioned load, net-metering rules, vendor availability, technical specifications, pre-existing solar systems, loan/RESCO mode and any 2025 amendments must be checked live. Additional State subsidy may exist but is routed through/integrated with the National Portal and cannot be assumed.
schemes.exclusions_text: Installations outside the approved portal/vendor/DISCOM process, non-residential connections, ineligible equipment, incomplete inspection/net-metering or non-compliant systems may not receive CFA. Subsidy is not paid merely for purchasing panels; the current guidelines require installation, verification and portal documentation. CFA limits and technical rules can change.
schemes.documents_required: Recent electricity bill/consumer number, DISCOM connection details, applicant identity/mobile/email, bank account and IFSC for subsidy, roof/property/site details and vendor quotation/installation information. Portal/DISCOM may request ownership/consent, net-metering forms and inspection documents.
schemes.conditional_documents: Aadhaar/PAN/KYC, cancelled cheque, property/roof consent, load enhancement or net-metering application, RWA authorization and common-facility documents, loan documents or RESCO agreement may be required depending on consumer/DISCOM/vendor route.
schemes.application_mode: Direct online application on the National Rooftop Solar/PM Surya Ghar portal with DISCOM assistance; field DISCOM helpdesks assist consumers who cannot complete the portal. Vendor selection and installation are consumer-facing steps, while subsidy release follows DISCOM verification.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Visit https://pmsuryaghar.gov.in/ or the National Rooftop Solar portal and register using the electricity consumer/DISCOM details. 2) Submit rooftop-solar application and wait for DISCOM technical approval. 3) Select an empanelled vendor and agree the discovered price/specification. 4) Vendor installs the system and uploads installation/PCR details. 5) Complete DISCOM inspection, net-metering and commissioning. 6) Upload/verify bank details and request CFA; track approval/release on the portal.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No recurring annual renewal for a commissioned installation; application and CFA are subject to the live scheme budget, portal window, DISCOM approval and current technical guidelines. Consumer must continue complying with DISCOM/net-metering rules.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track application, vendor, DISCOM approval, inspection and subsidy status on the National Portal. Use the DISCOM helpdesk/portal link, MNRE technical support (itsupport-mnre@nic.in) and the portal's escalation; vendor disputes should be raised with the DISCOM/MNRE grievance route.
schemes.source_authority: MNRE operational guidelines and National Rooftop Solar/PM Surya Ghar portal; DISCOM approvals and commissioning records control subsidy eligibility
schemes.next_review_action: For each pilot State, capture DISCOM link, consumer-load/net-metering requirements, current vendor list, portal amendment and subsidy-status workflow before presenting a final application checklist.
