schemes.scheme_name: NALSA free legal services / legal aid application
schemes.jurisdiction: India; legal services institutions at national, State, district, taluk, High Court and Supreme Court levels
schemes.administering_body: National Legal Services Authority under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, with State Legal Services Authorities, District/Taluk Legal Services Committees and High/Supreme Court Legal Services Committees
schemes.benefit_summary: Free legal advice, assistance, representation, drafting, process and related legal services for eligible applicants; institutions bear prescribed legal-service costs. Eligible applicants can seek help at any stage, including advice before filing, trial or appeal. Urgent guidance is available through NALSA helpline 15100.
schemes.eligibility_text: Section 12 categories include members of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes; victims of trafficking or begar; women or children; persons with disabilities/mental illness; victims of mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster; industrial workmen; persons in custody/protective or juvenile/psychiatric institutions; and persons below the applicable annual-income ceiling. Income ceilings vary by State/UT for non-Supreme-Court cases; the NALSA FAQ states less than ₹5 lakh for Supreme Court matters. Women and children qualify by category, not by a general income test.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The authority must determine territorial/subject-matter jurisdiction, current State income ceiling, proof/category sufficiency and whether the matter has a prima facie basis or is an abuse of process. Senior-citizen eligibility can depend on State rules. Legal aid is not an outcome guarantee and can be withdrawn under the regulations.
schemes.exclusions_text: Applicants outside Section 12 and above the applicable income ceiling may not receive full free representation, although legal advice/assistance may still be available at the institution's discretion. Abuse of process, false information, duplicate/withdrawn matters or failure to cooperate can lead to rejection/withdrawal. Normal court jurisdiction and case-law limits still apply.
schemes.documents_required: Application details: name, gender, permanent/contact address, phone/email, employment/nationality, nature of the legal problem, brief case statement and requested relief. Provide identity proof, category certificate where relevant (SC/ST/disability/custody etc.), income affidavit/certificate and relevant case notices/orders/documents. A plain-paper or oral application can be assisted by a paralegal volunteer.
schemes.conditional_documents: Court papers, FIR/complaint, notices, medical/disability certificate, caste/tribe certificate, custody proof, disaster/atrocity evidence, employment proof and income affidavit are conditional on the eligibility route and matter. The institution may ask for translations or certified copies.
schemes.application_mode: Online via NALSA/LSMS link, email, post, plain-paper application or in person at the appropriate TLSC/DLSA/SLSA/HCLSC/SCLSC front office. Applications are free; illiterate applicants may receive help from legal-aid officers/para-legal volunteers.

schemes.administering_body: Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes Department, Government of Haryana; District Welfare Officer/SCBC field offices
schemes.benefit_summary: Rs 80,000 household grant for repair/renovation of an old house. The official citizen page states annual family income up to Rs 1.80 lakh, Haryana domicile, house in applicant’s name and at least 10 years old. An August 2026 official PRMS release says the benefit is to resume from 25 September 2026 and notes expansion to poor families of all sections, but also refers to SC families; current scope must be confirmed.
schemes.eligibility_text: Permanent Haryana resident; annual family income not over Rs 1.80 lakh; house in applicant’s name and at least 10 years old; no previous house-repair grant from another department. Legacy implementation required SC/BPL status; the current August 2026 release says expansion to all poor sections while separately saying the scheme will resume for poor SC families.

schemes.exclusions_text: House not owned by applicant, house under 10 years, income above notified ceiling, prior repair grant, non-Haryana domicile, false ownership/income records or incomplete inspection documents exclude the application.
schemes.documents_required: Plot registry/ownership proof; Haryana residence/domicile proof; Aadhaar-linked bank account/passbook; Detailed repair estimate; Photographs of current house condition; Family ID/PPP and current income record
schemes.conditional_documents: SC/caste certificate and BPL ration card if required by the reopened category rules; House tax/land record or Lal Dora ownership proof; Death certificate for widow/orphan route if applicable; Additional inspection or Panchayat verification requested by DWO

schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No final 2026 closing date located. Official PRMS says scheme resumes 25 September 2026; older cycles had separate closure dates. Apply only during the reopened window; no annual renewal after one approved grant.

schemes.scheme_name: Mukhya Mantri Vivah Shagun Yojana
schemes.administering_body: Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes Department, Government of Haryana; District Welfare Officer/Additional Deputy Commissioner; SARAL/shaadi.e-Disha
schemes.benefit_summary: Grant varies by category: Rs 71,000 for SC/Denotified/Tapriwas communities living below BPL; Rs 51,000 for widow/divorced/destitute/orphan/destitute-child categories meeting the income/BPL rule and mass marriages; Rs 31,000 for sportswomen, all non-SC BPL sections and certain Divyangjan cases; Rs 51,000 where both newly married spouses are disabled and Rs 31,000 where one is disabled. The official page also lists Rs 1,100 plus sweet box for other Haryana couples registering within 30 days.
schemes.eligibility_text: Applicant generally applies for a daughter’s marriage before the marriage date. Category-specific conditions include BPL or annual family income below Rs 1 lakh for widow/divorced/destitute/orphan route; SC/DT/Tapriwas BPL; BPL non-SC; sportswoman (any caste/income); family income below Rs 1.80 lakh for the listed all-section category; mass marriage; or Divyangjan status. The couple must meet marriage/legal and Haryana/category documentation rules.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The page’s category (v) row omits the amount in the table; confirm whether the Rs 31,000/Rs 51,000 amount applies. Confirm current age, residence, income and marriage-registration requirements in the latest notification, because linked notifications are from 2021/2022.
schemes.exclusions_text: Application after three months from marriage is not entertained. Duplicate benefits under a similar scheme, failure of BPL/income/category proof, invalid marriage/registration, false documents, or missing post-marriage certificate can exclude or reduce payment.
schemes.documents_required: Haryana Family ID/PPP and identity/Aadhaar; Marriage invitation/proposed marriage details and bride’s identity/age proof; Marriage registration certificate for the post-marriage instalment; BPL ration card or current income certificate as applicable; Caste/DT/Tapriwas certificate where relevant; Haryana residence proof and bank account details
schemes.conditional_documents: Widow/divorce/destitute/orphan/dependent-child proof; Sports certificate for sportswoman category; Disability certificate for Divyangjan category; Mass-marriage organiser certificate; Death/guardian/relationship proof where parents are absent
schemes.application_mode: Online only through SARAL/Antyodaya; the RTS page identifies https://shaadi.edisha.gov.in as the online route, while the scheme page directs applicants to SARAL and Antyodaya Kendra assistance.
schemes.application_steps: Select the correct category and apply before the marriage date through SARAL/shaadi.e-Disha.; Upload PPP, identity, residence, category/BPL/income and proposed marriage documents.; After sanction/payment before marriage, complete the marriage registration promptly.; Upload the registration certificate within six months for the deferred Rs 3,000/Rs 5,000 component where applicable.; Track status and correct defects; no application is accepted after three months from marriage.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Apply before marriage. If filed after marriage, DWO may approve up to two months after marriage and Director HQ up to three months; nothing is entertained after three months. Post-marriage certificate must be submitted within six months for the deferred component.
schemes.tracking_grievance: RTS limit 30 working days; designated DWO, first appeal Additional Deputy Commissioner, second appeal Deputy Commissioner. Apply/track on shaadi.e-Disha/SARAL; Antyodaya Kendra can assist.

schemes.scheme_name: Educated Youth Allowance and Honorarium Scheme (Saksham Yuva)
schemes.administering_body: Directorate of Employment under Youth Empowerment and Entrepreneurship Department, Government of Haryana
schemes.benefit_summary: Unemployment allowance historically Rs 3,000/month for postgraduates, Rs 1,500/month for graduates and Rs 900/month for 10+2 applicants, plus honorarium for up to 100 hours’ honorary work (historically Rs 6,000/month for PG/graduate/10+2). A July 2026 official release says CET-qualified youth will receive 100 hours’ work and, if they do not receive employment for two years, allowance under Saksham Yuva from 1 November; this may add a new route and needs operational rules.
schemes.eligibility_text: Core official scheme PDF: Haryana domicile; registered on the live Employment Exchange (or register through HREX); qualifying postgraduate/graduate degree through eligible regular institutions or 10+2 from specified boards/schools in Haryana/UT Chandigarh; age 18–35 for 10+2 and 21–35 for graduate/postgraduate. Applicant must be unemployed and satisfy the scheme’s income/property, non-student, non-apprentice, non-self-employed and non-conviction conditions.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm the current allowance rates, whether 10+2 remains open, current family-income/property ceiling, CET two-year work requirement and how new CET-qualified youth are onboarded. The detailed PDF is older while the July 2026 official press release announces a new implementation route.
schemes.exclusions_text: Non-Haryana domicile, age outside the applicable band, unrecognized qualification, not on a live employment register, employment/self-employment/student/apprentice status, disqualifying government dismissal/conviction, income/property above current ceiling, duplicate unemployment allowance or failure to perform assigned honorary work can exclude/stop payment.
schemes.documents_required: Haryana domicile/residence proof; Educational certificates/marksheets; Employment Exchange/HREX registration number; Aadhaar/identity and bank account; Family income/property self-declaration as required; Recent photograph/mobile/email
schemes.conditional_documents: CET score/registration and work-assignment documents for the 2026 route; Degree regular-course proof; Category/board verification documents; Honorary-work attendance/assignment records
schemes.application_mode: Create/register as job seeker on the official HREX portal; apply for Saksham Yuva through the HREX scheme workflow after Employment Exchange registration. Confirm the new CET-specific route when the AI/work portal is published.
schemes.application_steps: Register as a Haryana job seeker at HREX and ensure the Employment Exchange record is live.; Complete Saksham Yuva application, qualification, bank and self-declaration fields and upload evidence.; Await department verification/approval and assignment of honorary work or skill training.; Complete up to 100 hours’ assigned work and submit attendance/claim as required.; Track allowance/honorarium and immediately report employment, study, self-employment or other ineligibility.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No fixed annual deadline in the current portal. Registration/allowance continues subject to annual verification and scheme rules; July 2026 press release says the CET-linked allowance starts 1 November after two years without employment, but precise claim deadline is not yet published.
schemes.tracking_grievance: HREX job-seeker account and district Employment Exchange; HREX field-office contacts are listed on the official site. Use HREX Directorate support and Mukhya Mantri Sewa Sankalp 1100 for unresolved cases.

schemes.scheme_name: Mukhya Mantri Kanyadan Yojana
schemes.administering_body: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment / Women and Child Development, Government of Himachal Pradesh; Child Development Project Officer (CDPO)/District Programme Officer
schemes.benefit_summary: Current official 2023-24 departmental plan states a Rs 51,000 marriage grant for a girl whose father or both parents are deceased, father is physically/mentally incapacitated or bedridden due to prolonged illness, mother is deserted/divorced, or the girl is/formerly was in a State Home/Nari Seva Sadan/Child Care Institution with no regular income. Annual income ceiling is stated as Rs 50,000 excluding MNREGA income. Older pages still show Rs 25,000 and Rs 35,000.
schemes.eligibility_text: Girl must fall into one of the destitute/fatherless/incapacitated-parent/deserted-mother/state-home/CCI categories, be a Himachal resident as required, have no regular income/support in the applicable category, and family annual income must not exceed Rs 50,000 excluding MNREGA income under the current plan document. Groom should be at least 21 in the 2021 notification materials.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Resolve the current amount/income threshold against the latest WCD/SJ&E notification: older official departmental scheme says Rs 25,000 and Rs 35,000, while the 2023-24 plan says Rs 51,000 and Rs 50,000. Confirm marriage-before/after application timing and whether the state-home/CCI route has separate documents.
schemes.exclusions_text: Income above current threshold, no qualifying destitution/parent condition, non-Himachal residence, groom under 21, duplicate Shagun benefit, false documents or failure to use the grant for marriage within three months can exclude/recover the grant. Applicant may use only one of Kanyadan or Shagun.
schemes.documents_required: Himachal bonafide/residence proof; Bride’s age/date-of-birth proof; Marriage registration certificate if marriage has occurred; Income certificate; Bank account details; Prescribed application form; Groom’s name/address and age proof
schemes.conditional_documents: Death certificates/non-traceable certificate for deceased/missing parents; Medical incapacity/bedridden certificate for father; Desertion/divorce proof for mother; State Home/Nari Seva Sadan/CCI residency certificate; BPL certificate if the local notification requires it
schemes.application_mode: Offline/department-assisted through Anganwadi/CDPO/District Programme Officer, with prescribed form and verification; the current e-District service list should be checked for any migrated online service.
schemes.application_steps: Obtain the current Kanyadan form and confirm the amount/income rule with CDPO/DPO.; Collect residence, age, income, bank and qualifying parent/destitution documents.; Submit to the CDPO/Anganwadi/District Programme Officer before marriage where required; submit marriage certificate after marriage if the notification permits post-event filing.; CDPO/field staff verify and sanction; receive grant by DBT/department process.; Use the grant for marriage within the required three-month period and retain proof.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No fixed annual deadline found. Timing is notification-specific; 2021 materials require marriage-related proof and say grant unused for three months must be refunded. Confirm the current submission window.
schemes.tracking_grievance: CDPO/District Programme Officer and District Welfare Officer; use Himachal Mukhya Mantri Sewa Sankalp 1100/e-District grievance if the service is migrated.

schemes.scheme_name: Himachal Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for SC/ST/OBC Students (e-Kalyan/NSP workflow)
schemes.administering_body: Directorate of Higher Education, Government of Himachal Pradesh; ESOMSA/e-Kalyan for welfare information and National Scholarship Portal (NSP) for current applications/verification; institutions and district/state nodal officers
schemes.benefit_summary: Post-matric scholarship provides maintenance/academic allowance and fee support subject to the applicable SC, ST or OBC/PM-YASASVI rules, course group and income ceiling. Official HP status reports list Post-Matric SC, Post-Matric ST and PM-YASASVI Post-Matric OBC/EBC/DNT as active scheme records; current applications are routed through NSP, not the generic ESOMSA landing page.
schemes.eligibility_text: Student must belong to the applicable SC/ST/OBC (or OBC/EBC/DNT PM-YASASVI) category, be a Himachal bonafide/resident where state implementation applies, be enrolled in an eligible recognised post-matric course/institution and satisfy the current parental-income/course/academic rules. Older HP official material states SC/ST parents’ income up to Rs 2 lakh; current central/PM-YASASVI rules may differ, so NSP’s scheme record governs.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm current AY 2026-27 category-wise income ceilings, course groups, rates, HP domicile rule and whether every category uses NSP or a specific e-Kalyan/department workflow. The ESOMSA e-Kalyan portal advertises general educational support but does not expose a specific HP post-matric application form; HP Higher Education notices repeatedly direct applicants to NSP.
schemes.exclusions_text: Wrong category, income above current ceiling, non-recognised course/institution, non-Himachal/non-applicable domicile, duplicate scholarship, incomplete Aadhaar/bank seeding, failure of institute/DNO verification or false certificates excludes or delays the claim.
schemes.documents_required: Caste/category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EBC/DNT as applicable); Himachal bonafide/domicile certificate where required; Current parental income certificate; Previous marksheet and current admission/bonafide certificate; Fee receipt/course and institution details; Aadhaar/OTR and Aadhaar-seeded bank account; Mobile/email and photograph
schemes.conditional_documents: Disability certificate for disability allowance; Hostel certificate; Family ID/PPP if HP verification requests it; Renewal scholarship ID/previous sanction and continuation certificate; DigiLocker or other digital verification documents
schemes.application_mode: Online fresh/renewal through the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) under the HP state/centrally sponsored scheme; institution and district/state nodal officers verify. Use ESOMSA/e-Kalyan/Him Access only for welfare information or if HP issues a specific migrated service.
schemes.application_steps: Check the latest HP Higher Education notice and NSP scheme list for the current academic year/category.; Create/maintain NSP OTR and verify Aadhaar/mobile/bank seeding.; Select HP Post-Matric SC, ST or applicable OBC/PM-YASASVI scheme, complete academic/category/income fields and upload documents.; Submit before the active NSP deadline; print/save application ID and ask institution to verify.; Resolve defects, monitor institute/DNO/state status and payment; correct Aadhaar-seeding issues if flagged.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No AY 2026-27 deadline found in the reviewed HP notice excerpts. AY 2025-26 HP notices used NSP and had academic-year-specific deadlines/extensions; renewal is required each year. Do not use an old deadline.
schemes.tracking_grievance: NSP application/status and institution nodal officer; HP Directorate of Higher Education scholarship contact 0177-2656622 and dhe-sml-hp@gov.in; HP notices also reference nsphpsml@gmail.com. ESOMSA/Him Access and Mukhya Mantri Sewa Sankalp 1100 can route welfare/identity grievances.

schemes.scheme_name: Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board Shagun Scheme
schemes.administering_body: Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Department of Labour, Government of Punjab; district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner with SDM/DC approval for this high-value scheme
schemes.benefit_summary: Rs 51,000 for marriage-related expenses. The 2026 Board handbook states Rs 21,000 where Punjab Government Ashirwad Scheme assistance is also taken; otherwise Rs 51,000. Maximum two daughters’ marriages per registered worker.
schemes.eligibility_text: Applicant must be a registered Punjab BOCW construction worker at the marriage. A registered worker may apply for up to two unmarried daughters, or for the second marriage of a widowed/divorced daughter. An unmarried, widowed or divorced female registered worker may apply for her own marriage. Marriage must be supported by a marriage certificate from the Registrar of Marriages or a religious institution. Application must be filed within one year of the marriage or within one year of issue of the government marriage certificate, as applicable.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm live portal field rules for the second-marriage case, whether the one-year period is calculated from ceremony or certificate where both dates differ, and the Ashirwad overlap/reduced amount logic. A 2020 official Punjab form says three months, conflicting with the 2026 handbook’s one year; current handbook should control but the portal/circular should be checked.
schemes.exclusions_text: Maximum two daughters; parents cannot claim for a daughter if the registered daughter herself claims; unregistered worker; marriage outside the covered categories; missing/invalid marriage proof; late application; duplicate claim; and any claim barred by the live BOCW rules or Ashirwad overlap.
schemes.documents_required: BOCW registration/member details; marriage certificate from Registrar of Marriages or religious institution; Aadhaar of bride and groom; bride photograph; wedding photograph of bride and groom; bank passbook or cancelled cheque; applicant self-declaration.
schemes.conditional_documents: Proof of widow/divorce status for a second marriage; Ashirwad Scheme sanction/non-availment information; nominee/family documents if applicant is a successor; any portal-requested residence or relationship proof.
schemes.application_mode: Online through the Punjab Kirti Sahayak mobile app or Punjab BOCW portal; obtain assistance from the district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner if online filing fails. The scheme remains one of the high-value claims requiring SDM/DC approval.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm active BOCW registration and mobile/Aadhaar linkage. 2) Open Punjab Kirti Sahayak or the BOCW portal and choose Shagun. 3) Enter worker, bride/groom, marriage and bank details. 4) Upload the certificate, Aadhaar, photographs, passbook/cancelled cheque and declaration. 5) Submit and retain acknowledgement/file number. 6) Respond to objections and follow the Labour Inspector to SDM/DC approval. 7) Track status online until DBT/payment.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: File within one year of marriage or government marriage-certificate issue under the current 2026 handbook; no annual renewal after sanction, but the two-daughter cap applies.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Check file status by registration number, Aadhaar or mobile at https://bocw1.punjab.gov.in/bapi/worker/status; escalate to the district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner, Punjab BOCW head office Labour Bhawan Sector 64 Mohali (0172-2702486/0172-2211755), then Labour Department grievance channels.
schemes.source_authority: Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board 2026 handbook; Punjab Labour Department; Government of Punjab BOCW portal/app; older official form retained only to document the date-rule conflict
schemes.next_review_action: Verify the live Shagun form and deadline in Kirti Sahayak/BOCW portal and obtain the latest Board circular on Ashirwad overlap before production guidance.

schemes.scheme_name: Punjab BOCW Education Assistance/Stipend for Workers’ Children
schemes.administering_body: Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Department of Labour, Government of Punjab; district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner and education/institution verification systems
schemes.benefit_summary: Annual education assistance for registered workers’ children and, in limited cases, the worker’s own evening study. The 2026 handbook gives course/gender-linked assistance broadly from Rs 3,000 to Rs 70,000 per year, including school, graduation/post-graduation, ITI/polytechnic, medical/engineering and professional courses; hostel-linked rates are higher. Exact amount must be selected from the live course table.
schemes.eligibility_text: Child of a registered Punjab BOCW worker, or a registered worker attending evening classes. Worker must be registered; student must have passed the previous class/examination and be admitted to the current class/course. Application is due within one year of admission. If both parents are registered, only one parent may apply. The handbook covers school through graduate, postgraduate, technical and professional study. The former 50% attendance condition was waived by the Board circular dated 7 November 2025.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm the exact current rate/course mapping for every course, whether private/recognized institutions are accepted in all categories, treatment of repeaters and distance learning, and the live portal’s two-child/course restrictions. Verify the 2025 attendance waiver remains active for the application year.
schemes.exclusions_text: Unregistered worker; student who did not pass the previous class; duplicate parent claim where both parents are registered; duplicate scholarship for the same course/year; unrecognised institution/course; late application; incomplete or mismatched academic/Aadhaar data; and claims outside the current handbook table.
schemes.documents_required: Worker-signed Form 27 or online equivalent; student Aadhaar; previous-class pass certificate/marksheet; current-class or admission certificate; student photograph; self-declaration; bank details where requested.
schemes.conditional_documents: Hostel certificate for hosteller rate; fee/admission receipt; institution verification; extra academic proof where education-data integration does not verify the student. For Punjab government/government-aided schools, student Aadhaar may auto-populate records; an unverified record is handled manually and should not by itself penalise the applicant.
schemes.application_mode: Online through Punjab Kirti Sahayak app or Punjab BOCW portal, with institution/education verification where applicable; district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner can assist with objections or manual processing.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Check active BOCW membership and parent/student Aadhaar data. 2) Select Education/Stipend in Kirti Sahayak or the BOCW portal. 3) Select student, class/session/course and hosteller status. 4) Upload Form 27/equivalent, marksheet, current admission proof, photograph, declaration and conditional hostel/fee proof. 5) Final-submit and save the file number. 6) Respond to any institution or Labour Department objection. 7) Track approval and DBT/payment.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Apply within one year of admission. Education support is annual and normally requires a fresh/renewal claim for each academic year under the live portal rules.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Use https://bocw1.punjab.gov.in/bapi/worker/status with registration number, Aadhaar or mobile; escalate through the institution, Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner, Punjab BOCW head office Labour Bhawan Sector 64 Mohali and Punjab Labour Department.

schemes.next_review_action: Capture the live portal’s course/rate table and current academic-session notice, and test one verified and one unverified education record before exposing amount recommendations.

schemes.scheme_name: Punjab BOCW Ex-Gratia / Accidental Death and Permanent Disability Assistance
schemes.administering_body: Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Department of Labour, Government of Punjab; district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner, SDM/DC approval for ex-gratia claims
schemes.benefit_summary: Current 2026 Board handbook: Rs 4,00,000 for accidental death; Rs 2,00,000 for natural death; permanent disability at Rs 4,000 per certified percentage up to Rs 4,00,000. Death assistance is to be disbursed within 60 days under the handbook workflow when the claim is complete.
schemes.eligibility_text: Worker must have been registered with the Punjab BOCW Board at death or at the time of disability; the handbook specifies worker age 18–59 for this claim. Nominee may apply; if the nominee has died, an eligible family member applies. A minor child’s benefit is placed in an FDR until age 18. For death, apply within one year of death. For permanent disability, apply within one year of the Civil Surgeon disability-certificate issue. Permanent disability must be certified by a Civil Surgeon.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm the exact definition of accidental versus natural death, registration/grace-period wording in the live form, nominee/family priority rules, treatment of death during lapsed registration where arrears are payable, and whether disability percentage is rounded or capped by the portal.
schemes.exclusions_text: Unregistered worker at the relevant event; death/disability outside the covered definitions; missing Civil Surgeon certificate or death/accident evidence; late claim; duplicate claim; ineligible successor/nominee; and false or incomplete documents. Minor-child handling and family succession follow Board verification.
schemes.documents_required: Death certificate; Aadhaar of deceased worker and applicant; bank passbook/cancelled cheque; self-declaration; BOCW registration/member record. For accidental death, FIR and post-mortem report. For permanent disability, Civil Surgeon disability certificate and worker Aadhaar/bank proof.
schemes.conditional_documents: Nomination proof; legal-heir/family relationship and death certificate of a nominee who died; family NOC where required; guardian and FDR documents for minor child; registration renewal/arrears receipts; employer/accident records if the Board requests them.
schemes.application_mode: Online through Punjab Kirti Sahayak app or BOCW portal, followed by district Labour Department scrutiny and SDM/DC approval because ex-gratia is a high-value exception to the simplified approval route. District office/manual help is available.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm worker registration and nominee record. 2) File Ex-Gratia/Death or Permanent Disability claim in Kirti Sahayak/BOCW portal. 3) Upload event certificate and identity/bank documents, plus FIR/post-mortem or Civil Surgeon certificate as applicable. 4) Submit within the one-year window and retain acknowledgement. 5) Cooperate with Labour Inspector/ALC verification and SDM/DC approval. 6) Track file and DBT/payment; for a minor, confirm FDR details.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Death claim within one year of death; disability claim within one year of disability-certificate issue. No annual renewal of a death claim; worker registration itself must have been valid or regularised according to the Board’s current rules.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Status by registration number, Aadhaar or mobile: https://bocw1.punjab.gov.in/bapi/worker/status. Escalate to district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner, then Punjab BOCW head office Labour Bhawan Sector 64 Mohali and Labour Department grievance channels.

schemes.next_review_action: Verify the current portal’s nominee/legal-heir checklist and capture a current Board circular defining accident proof, grace periods and the 60-day service standard.

schemes.scheme_name: Post-Matric Scholarship for Students with Disabilities (Chandigarh applicants)
schemes.jurisdiction: Chandigarh UT routing through the National Scholarship Portal
schemes.administering_body: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Government of India; National Scholarship Portal; Chandigarh Administration Education Department as UT/institution nodal verification authority
schemes.benefit_summary: For Class XI-XII, diploma/degree and postgraduate study. DEPwD’s current scheme page lists tuition/admission fee support up to Rs 1,40,000, other fee up to Rs 10,000, book allowance Rs 1,500/year, disability allowance Rs 2,000–4,000/year, and maintenance support of Rs 1,200/month for hostellers or Rs 650/month for day scholars for 12 months, subject to the current guideline and course ceilings.
schemes.eligibility_text: Indian national studying Class XI or XII, diploma, degree or postgraduate course in a recognised institution; benchmark disability of at least 40%; UDID card; annual family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh; and no other post-matric scholarship or stipend. Maximum two children with disabilities from the same parents may receive the scholarship. Chandigarh’s 2018 official notice additionally described the route for permanent Chandigarh residents and institution submission, but current central/NSP rules should be checked for domicile treatment.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm Chandigarh domicile/residence requirement under the current 2026 UT nodal instructions, exact course-group fee ceilings, renewal/academic-performance rules, and whether any institution or category exceptions apply. The older Chandigarh notice is 2018-19; it is evidence of local routing, not a current deadline.
schemes.exclusions_text: Disability below benchmark threshold; income above Rs 2.5 lakh; non-Indian; unrecognised course/institution; duplicate post-matric scholarship/stipend; more than two sibling beneficiaries; incomplete UDID/Aadhaar/bank or institutional verification; and late/defective NSP application.
schemes.documents_required: Student photograph; Aadhaar; UDID card or UDID enrolment plus disability certificate; parent/guardian income certificate; last academic qualification marksheet; current admission/enrolment and tuition-fee receipt; student bank passbook/account details; age/identity proof where requested.

schemes.scheme_name: Chandigarh Post-Matric Scholarship for SC Students and OBC/PM-YASASVI Route
schemes.jurisdiction: Chandigarh UT; Chandigarh-domiciled SC/OBC/EBC students and Chandigarh institutions
schemes.administering_body: Directorate of Higher Education, Chandigarh Administration; Government of India sponsoring departments; National Scholarship Portal/Chandigarh ServiceOnline and institution nodal officers
schemes.benefit_summary: Post-matric financial assistance for eligible Chandigarh SC students and the current OBC/EBC route. Chandigarh’s official guidance identifies Class 10+1 onward, passed previous examination and family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh for both SC and OBC/EBC tracks. The OBC post-matric scheme was merged into PM-YASASVI; amount/course-group rates and reimbursement rules are controlled by the current scheme notification.
schemes.eligibility_text: For PMS-SC: Indian student belonging to a recognised SC community, bonafide Chandigarh resident, studying a recognised post-matric/post-secondary course from Class XI onward, and passed the previous examination; official Chandigarh guidance states annual family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh. For OBC/EBC: Chandigarh-bonafide OBC/EBC student in post-matric study, passed previous examination and income up to Rs 2.5 lakh under the Chandigarh guidance; the OBC post-matric and Dr Ambedkar EBC route has been merged into PM-YASASVI. Institution, domicile and current central course rules also apply.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: No current 2026 Chandigarh notice was found that confirms the PMS-SC opening date, current amount table, whether the application is on NSP or ServiceOnline/another Chandigarh workflow, domicile certificate format, attendance/renewal rules, or whether PM-YASASVI’s current college/school sub-scheme is the correct OBC route for the applicant. The accessible Chandigarh notice is for session 2022-23 and must not be treated as a current deadline.
schemes.exclusions_text: Non-SC/non-OBC/EBC applicant; non-Chandigarh domicile where domicile is required; income above the applicable ceiling; failed previous examination; unrecognised course/institution; duplicate scholarship or incompatible stipend; incomplete caste/income/bank/academic records; late or unverified application; and any current PM-YASASVI course/institution merit conditions.
schemes.documents_required: SC caste certificate or Chandigarh-recognised OBC/EBC certificate; Chandigarh domicile/residence proof; parent/guardian income certificate; Aadhaar/identity; previous examination marksheet; current admission/enrolment and institution details; student bank account/passbook for DBT; photograph; undertaking and fee/course details as requested.
schemes.conditional_documents: Fee receipt/freeship or reimbursement documents; hostel certificate; renewal/previous scholarship ID; institution hard-copy checklist; OBC non-creamy-layer evidence if required by the current PM-YASASVI notice; disability or other category proof only where a separate linked benefit is claimed.

schemes.scheme_name: Free Legal Aid through State Legal Services Authority, UT Chandigarh
schemes.administering_body: State Legal Services Authority, UT Chandigarh; District Legal Services Authority Chandigarh; National Legal Services Authority under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
schemes.benefit_summary: Free legal advice, counselling and representation in civil/criminal and other proceedings; panel advocate, drafting/translation, process and witness expenses, certified copies and other approved legal costs. Legal services can also help beneficiaries access government welfare schemes and can support Lok Adalat/mediation routes.
schemes.eligibility_text: Eligible under Section 12 include: SC/ST member; trafficking/begar victim; woman or child; mentally ill or otherwise disabled person; victim of mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster; industrial workman; person in custody/protective or juvenile home/psychiatric institution; or a person whose annual income is below the prescribed ceiling. NALSA’s current table lists Chandigarh UT income ceiling at Rs 3,00,000 per year for cases before courts other than the Supreme Court; Supreme Court matters use the Rs 5,00,000 ceiling. A genuine case is also required under Section 13.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm whether a specific matter falls under DLSA Chandigarh, SLSA Chandigarh, High Court Legal Services Committee or another authority; confirm any case-type/document requirements and whether a current Chandigarh notification has raised the income ceiling. Women and children qualify by category irrespective of income according to NALSA guidance, but the authority still screens the case.
schemes.exclusions_text: Applicant outside Section 12 categories and above the applicable income ceiling; no genuine case; misrepresentation/fraud; non-cooperation; engaging another lawyer after assignment; death where proceedings do not survive; or abuse of legal-services process. Legal aid may be denied/withdrawn subject to appeal to the authority’s Chairman/Executive Chairman.
schemes.documents_required: Identity and contact proof; brief facts and relief sought; case/notice/FIR/court papers if any; SC/ST, disability, custody, workman or disaster proof where relying on a category; income details and affidavit where applying under income category; address/residence; relevant orders, dates and prior lawyer information.
schemes.conditional_documents: Income affidavit is generally sufficient unless questioned; custody/juvenile or medical certificate; woman/child or trafficking proof where requested; certified copies, witness details and any legal notice. Illiterate applicants may apply orally and a paralegal volunteer/officer can complete the form.
schemes.application_mode: Online through NALSA’s Legal Aid Application/LACMS portal, by email or written application, or orally/in person at the SLSA/DLSA front office. Chandigarh SLSA also provides 1516 legal-assistance, 15100 national legal-aid and 24x7 mobile legal-advice channels.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Gather identity, case papers and category/income proof. 2) Apply online at the NALSA legal-aid application link, or visit DLSA/SLSA front office at District Courts Sector 43 or Additional Deluxe Building Sector 9-D. 3) State the facts, legal issue, desired relief and preferred panel lawyer if any. 4) Submit/upload documents; an application number is generated for online cases. 5) Authority scrutinises eligibility and merits, normally deciding within seven days. 6) Track the application and contact the assigned lawyer; appeal or complain to the authority if denied or service is unsatisfactory.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No application deadline; online applications are available 24x7 and legal aid may be requested at any stage of a case. A decision should be taken immediately and no later than seven days under NALSA regulations; case-specific follow-up continues while proceedings remain active.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track using the online application number/LACMS; call Chandigarh SLSA 1516 or NALSA 15100, 24x7 advice +91-7087-112-348, office +91-172-2742999, or email slsa_utchd@yahoo.com. Appeal a denial to the Executive Chairman/Chairman and complain through NALSA/SLSA grievance channels.

schemes.next_review_action: Verify the current Chandigarh SLSA front-office hours and live LACMS form fields, and map case types to DLSA versus SLSA for the chatbot’s routing logic.

schemes.scheme_name: PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; urban local bodies and participating lenders, including vendors in surrounding peri-urban/rural areas who vend within eligible urban limits
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, implemented through ULBs/Town Vending Committees, SIDBI portal and participating banks/NBFCs/MFIs
schemes.benefit_summary: Collateral-free working-capital loans to eligible street vendors. The enhanced structure reported by MoHUA provides up to ₹15,000 first tranche, ₹25,000 second tranche and ₹50,000 third tranche, subject to repayment/eligibility. Timely repayment can unlock the next tranche; 7% interest subsidy and digital-transaction cashback apply under current scheme rules.
schemes.eligibility_text: Street vendors identified in the ULB/Town Vending Committee survey or holding a Certificate of Vending/Identity Card can apply. Vendors left out of the survey, and vendors from surrounding development/peri-urban/rural areas who vend within the ULB's geographical limits, may obtain a Letter of Recommendation from the ULB/TVC using proof of vending or local enquiry. The applicant must satisfy the lender's KYC and credit process.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The current enhanced tranche and coverage depend on the latest MoHUA circular/portal configuration and the vendor's prior-loan history. ULB verification, vending geography, CoV/ID/LoR and lender risk checks are decisive; portal submission is not a loan sanction.
schemes.exclusions_text: Applicants who are not genuine vendors, do not vend in the eligible urban/geographical area, cannot obtain CoV/ID/LoR, submit duplicate/false records or fail lender KYC/credit checks may be rejected. A lender may refuse even a portal-complete application under its credit policy. Tranche upgrades require timely repayment and current scheme conditions.
schemes.documents_required: Certificate of Vending/Identity Card or provisional CoV/LoR; Aadhaar, voter ID, driving licence, MGNREGA card or PAN as KYC; mobile number, bank account and basic vending/family details. Keep the loan application acknowledgement and lender account details.
schemes.conditional_documents: For surveyed vendors without a card, ULB may issue provisional CoV/ID. For unsurveyed vendors, past vending-loan records, membership in a street-vendor association or other vending proof/local enquiry can support an LoR. Lenders may request additional KYC, consent/e-KYC and credit-history authorization.
schemes.application_mode: Self/assisted application on the PM SVANidhi portal or through ULB/BC/agent of a participating bank, MFI or NBFC. The official FAQ says BC/MFI agents help fill/upload the loan application; loan sanction remains with the lender.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Check survey/CoV/ID status with the ULB/TVC or obtain an LoR. 2) Prepare KYC, mobile and bank details. 3) Apply at https://pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in/ or through an approved BC/MFI/bank agent. 4) Complete Aadhaar/e-KYC and lender checks. 5) Track sanction/disbursement and repay on schedule. 6) Use digital transactions to earn eligible cashback and apply for the next tranche after timely repayment.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No single national annual renewal is stated in the public FAQ; the current lending window and tranche rules are portal/notification dependent. Each tranche is a separate credit cycle and must be repaid according to its tenure before the next tranche.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Use the PM SVANidhi portal/app status and the lending institution/ULB. The official FAQ directs grievances to MoHUA's PM SVANidhi/NULM officers; portal support is available through portal.pmsvanidhi@sidbi.in. Preserve application and loan account numbers.

schemes.next_review_action: Confirm the current portal tranche values, eligible city/ULB list, Punjab/Haryana/Himachal/Chandigarh ULB contacts, approved lenders and live grievance route.

schemes.scheme_name: Stand-Up India Scheme
schemes.jurisdiction: India; Scheduled Commercial Banks and Stand-Up Mitra handholding portal
schemes.administering_body: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance; Scheduled Commercial Banks with SIDBI/Stand-Up Mitra ecosystem
schemes.benefit_summary: Composite bank loan from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for setting up a greenfield enterprise in manufacturing, services, trading or activities allied to agriculture. Repayment may extend up to seven years including up to 18 months moratorium. Margin-money support up to 15% may converge with eligible schemes, but the borrower must normally bring at least 10% own contribution.
schemes.eligibility_text: An individual entrepreneur above 18 years who is a woman or belongs to Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe may apply for a first-time/greenfield enterprise. For a non-individual enterprise, at least 51% of the shareholding and controlling stake should be held by an eligible woman or SC/ST entrepreneur under the scheme rules. The applicant and enterprise must satisfy the lender's KYC, project viability, credit and statutory requirements.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The DFS page confirms the route and loan range but current continuation/extension, credit-guarantee terms, exact promoter-contribution treatment and sector-specific bank criteria should be checked with the current Stand-Up Mitra/bank. It is a bank loan, not an assured grant or entitlement.
schemes.exclusions_text: Existing/expansion businesses that are not greenfield, applicants under 18, non-eligible category/control structures, projects outside permitted sectors, deficient own contribution, default/unsatisfactory credit or missing licences/project viability may be rejected. Final sanction rests with the Scheduled Commercial Bank.
schemes.documents_required: Identity/address proof, age, caste certificate for SC/ST applicants or woman-ownership/control details, PAN/KYC, bank statements, business constitution/registration, project report, quotations, premises/lease proof, licences/registrations, projected cash flow and promoter contribution evidence.
schemes.conditional_documents: Udyam/GST/shop licence, partnership/company incorporation and 51% ownership/control records, environmental/sector clearances, collateral/guarantee or credit-guarantee documents, and convergence-scheme paperwork are conditional on the project and lender.
schemes.application_mode: Online handholding and lender application through https://www.standupmitra.in or assisted at a participating Scheduled Commercial Bank branch. The portal guides, matches and tracks; the bank appraises and sanctions.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm eligible entrepreneur/category and a new greenfield project. 2) Prepare project report, promoter contribution and KYC/category documents. 3) Register on Stand-Up Mitra and use guidance/handholding or approach an SCB branch. 4) Select lender/sector and submit the composite-loan application. 5) Complete appraisal, statutory checks and sanction terms. 6) Accept only after reviewing rate, margin, repayment, moratorium and any security/guarantee conditions.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No rolling annual renewal is stated on the current DFS scheme page; apply while the scheme and lender window are active. Loan repayment and any working-capital renewal are lender-specific. A current extension/status check is required because public material has referred to continuation through 2025.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track on Stand-Up Mitra and with the assigned bank branch/nodal officer. Escalate bank service complaints through the bank's grievance channel, DFS/CPGRAMS and applicable RBI/Ombudsman route; the portal does not guarantee sanction.
schemes.source_authority: Department of Financial Services official scheme page and participating bank/Stand-Up Mitra materials; bank credit appraisal controls the application
schemes.next_review_action: Check Stand-Up Mitra live availability, current scheme extension, bank list, credit-guarantee/margin rules and the pilot States' nodal bank contacts.

schemes.scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; Ministry of Labour and Employment with CSCs, LIC/PFRDA implementation support and pension account providers
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of Labour and Employment; enrollment through Common Service Centres/self-registration and contributory pension infrastructure
schemes.benefit_summary: Voluntary contributory pension for eligible unorganised workers. After age 60, the subscriber receives an assured monthly pension of ₹3,000; spouse receives 50% family pension after subscriber death, and scheme rules govern return/continuation of contributions. Worker contribution is matched 1:1 by the Central Government and ranges from ₹55 to ₹200 per month based on entry age.
schemes.eligibility_text: An unorganised worker aged 18–40 with monthly income ₹15,000 or less may join. Examples include home-based workers, street vendors, head-loaders, brick-kiln workers, cobblers, rag pickers, domestic workers, washermen, rickshaw pullers, rural landless labourers, own-account workers, agricultural/construction/beedi/handloom/leather workers. The applicant must not be covered by EPFO, ESIC or a government-contributed NPS and must not be an income-tax payer.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The enrollment portal/CSC must validate occupation, income and exclusion status; e-Shram registration may assist but is not itself pension approval. Contribution, exit, missed-payment and spouse/family-pension treatment follow current PM-SYM rules and should be explained before consent.
schemes.exclusions_text: Persons outside 18–40, monthly income above ₹15,000, income-tax payers, EPFO/ESIC members or government-contributed NPS members are excluded from new enrollment. False declarations, duplicate accounts or prolonged non-payment can stop government matching/affect account status under the rules.
schemes.documents_required: Aadhaar, savings bank account or Jan Dhan account, mobile number, age/date-of-birth proof and nominee/spouse details; self-declaration of occupation, unorganised-worker status, income and non-membership/non-taxpayer status. CSC biometric/e-KYC is used for assisted enrollment.
schemes.conditional_documents: e-Shram/UAN, bank passbook, income/occupation or local vending/work evidence, spouse/nominee identity and guardian details may be requested for verification, corrections or family-pension claims.
schemes.application_mode: Self-registration online through the Maandhan portal or assisted enrollment at a CSC. The government services portal confirms both routes; the worker authorizes recurring auto-debit and matching contribution.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm age, income and statutory-scheme exclusions. 2) Visit https://maandhan.in or a CSC with Aadhaar, bank account and mobile. 3) Complete e-KYC and self-declarations, add spouse/nominee and authorize auto-debit. 4) Save the pension account/acknowledgement. 5) Fund the age-based monthly contribution and monitor the matching contribution. 6) Update bank/contact/nominee details and use the rules-based exit/death process if circumstances change.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No national application deadline; enrollment is open to eligible workers aged 18–40. Contributions recur until age 60 and are not a yearly re-application. Missed contributions, exit and restoration are governed by current scheme rules.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track through the Maandhan portal/CSC and the pension account provider. Seek help through Labour Ministry/CSC channels and the portal grievance route; preserve account number, debit records and consent.
schemes.source_authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment official FAQ, India Services portal and PM-SYM portal; CSC/account records control enrollment

schemes.scheme_name: National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) for SC, DNT/NT/SNT, landless agricultural labourer and traditional artisan candidates
schemes.jurisdiction: India; Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, with Indian Missions abroad for reimbursement
schemes.administering_body: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; Indian Missions abroad process tuition/maintenance reimbursements
schemes.benefit_summary: Financial assistance for eligible low-income meritorious candidates pursuing Master's or PhD study abroad. The 2026-27 scheme provides 125 annual slots (115 SC, 6 DNT/NT/SNT, 4 landless agricultural labourers/traditional artisans) with 30% earmarked for female candidates. Assistance includes tuition, maintenance and approved allowances paid through the Indian Mission/University process rather than a simple unrestricted cash grant.
schemes.eligibility_text: Candidate must belong to SC, De-notified/Nomadic/Semi-Nomadic Tribes, landless agricultural labourer or traditional artisan category; have at least 60%/equivalent in the qualifying examination; total family income below ₹8 lakh in the preceding financial year; be below 35 years on the scheme's prescribed date; and hold an unconditional admission offer to an eligible Master's or PhD course at a top-500 QS-ranked foreign university under the current guidelines. Selection is competitive and slot limited.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The exact 2026-27 guideline controls age reference date, eligible courses/fields, QS list, family-income composition, number of prior attempts, language/visa/medical requirements and category certificates. The portal may open multiple selection rounds, and an offer does not guarantee selection.
schemes.exclusions_text: Applicants outside the four categories, over the age limit, above the income ceiling, below the academic threshold, lacking an unconditional eligible foreign offer or applying after the round deadline are not eligible. Incomplete/false documents, duplicate applications, already funded overlapping scholarship or failure to obtain visa/offer conditions may prevent award or reimbursement.
schemes.documents_required: Caste/category certificate or prescribed landless agricultural labourer/traditional artisan certificate; marksheets/degree; age proof; income certificate/ITR/affidavit; unconditional admission offer; passport; bank details; photograph/signature; domicile/nationality and undertaking/consent documents. Upload formats and self-attestation follow the NOS portal guideline.
schemes.conditional_documents: University QS ranking/course proof, research proposal for PhD, recommendation/academic documents, disability/female/category evidence where applicable, visa/offer correspondence, passport/visa, medical/insurance and Indian Mission documents are conditional on award stage.
schemes.application_mode: Direct online application on the official NOS portal https://nosmsje.gov.in, with document upload and selection-round scrutiny. It is a competitive, time-window application; there is no automatic award after submitting.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Read the current 2026-27 guideline and confirm category, marks, income, age and course/university. 2) Obtain an unconditional offer and prepare certificates/passport/income documents. 3) Register on the NOS portal during an announced selection round. 4) Complete the application and upload legible documents before the deadline. 5) Track scrutiny/result and respond to corrections. 6) If selected, follow Ministry/Indian Mission instructions for visa, joining and reimbursement.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Selection-year windows are fixed and can be short. The NOS portal states the 2026-27 first-round application window was 24 April–2 June 2026, with a 4–7 June correction window and no new registrations during corrections. Future rounds/deadlines must be read from the live portal; renewal/continuation follows award conditions.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track application/results on https://nosmsje.gov.in, use portal notices/contact and the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment. After selection, contact the designated Indian Mission/Ministry desk for reimbursement and joining issues.

schemes.scheme_name: AICTE Pragati Scholarship Scheme for Girl Students (Technical Degree/Diploma)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; AICTE-approved technical institutions and National Scholarship Portal
schemes.administering_body: All India Council for Technical Education, Ministry of Education; applications and verification through the National Scholarship Portal and institutes
schemes.benefit_summary: Scholarship support for eligible girl students admitted to first-year AICTE-approved technical diploma or degree programmes. Official AICTE materials describe support up to ₹50,000 per annum, while older FAQs describe the tuition/actual-fee and replacement-expense treatment; the current NSP scheme specification controls the amount and components for the selected academic year.
schemes.eligibility_text: A girl student admitted to the first year of an AICTE-approved technical diploma or undergraduate degree course at an eligible institute may apply. Up to two girls per family and annual family income below ₹8 lakh are stated in AICTE's official FAQ; admission/seat route, institute/course approval, merit and current academic-year rules must be satisfied. Current NSP labels the degree and diploma variants separately.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The exact current scholarship amount, renewal criteria, admission quota restrictions, family-member cap and document list can change in the NSP/AICTE specification. Older AICTE FAQs contain historical academic-year wording and should not override the current 2026-27 NSP record.
schemes.exclusions_text: Students not in an AICTE-approved eligible technical programme, not in the permitted first-year/renewal stage, above the income limit, beyond the two-girls-per-family rule or submitting duplicate/inaccurate applications may be rejected. Management-quota/seat-route restrictions appear in older AICTE FAQs and require current specification confirmation.
schemes.documents_required: NSP One-Time Registration (OTR) number, Aadhaar/EID and identity, institute/admission proof, marksheet, family-income certificate, bank account/passbook seeded as required for DBT, photograph/signature and institute/course details. Upload current category/disability certificates only if the NSP specification requests them.
schemes.conditional_documents: Fee receipt/tuition-fee waiver proof, domicile/category certificate, parent declaration, renewal marks/attendance, and institute verification documents vary by academic year and application type.
schemes.application_mode: Online-only through the National Scholarship Portal with institute verification. From AY 2024-25, NSP OTR is mandatory; the institute must be registered/verified on NSP.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Generate NSP OTR at https://scholarships.gov.in/ and verify the institute/course. 2) Select the current AICTE Pragati Degree or Diploma scheme. 3) Complete fresh/renewal application and upload required documents. 4) Submit before the student deadline and get institute verification. 5) Correct defective applications within the correction window. 6) Track DNO/SNO/MNO verification and DBT sanction on NSP/PFMS.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: For AY 2026-27, NSP lists applications open 1 June–31 October 2026; defective and institute verification is listed through 15 November and DNO/SNO/MNO verification through 30 November 2026. These dates are current portal dates and may be extended; renewal is annual subject to current rules.

schemes.scheme_name: Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board Maternity Benefit Scheme
schemes.administering_body: Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Department of Labour, Government of Punjab; district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner
schemes.benefit_summary: Rs 21,000 per eligible delivery for a registered female construction worker and Rs 5,000 for a registered male worker/father, for up to two children, under the Board’s current scheme materials. Payment is made through the registered bank account.
schemes.eligibility_text: Registered Punjab BOCW beneficiary connected to the birth of an eligible child; the Board’s scheme is for up to two children. The female beneficiary may claim maternity assistance and the male registered worker may claim the father/paternity-linked amount for the newborn. The applicant must maintain active BOCW membership/contributions and submit the child’s registered birth certificate. The 2025 simplification announcement says the child’s birth certificate is sufficient for the core claim and removed the earlier child-Aadhaar requirement.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm the live portal’s definition of the first/two eligible children, whether the male claim requires proof that the mother is the worker’s spouse, minimum membership/contribution period, claim deadline after birth, and whether miscarriage/adoption or multiple-birth cases have special rules. The official 2020 Form 46 and 2019 notification are older than the 2025 simplification and should not override the live portal.
schemes.exclusions_text: Unregistered or lapsed worker; claim beyond the first two eligible children; duplicate claim for the same birth; missing/invalid birth certificate; inactive contributions; late or incomplete submission; and any claim not covered by the current Board’s maternity/paternity rules.
schemes.documents_required: BOCW registration/member number; child’s birth certificate issued by the Registrar; applicant Aadhaar/identity and bank details; application Form 46 or online equivalent; self-declaration where requested.
schemes.conditional_documents: Marriage/spouse proof for a male worker’s paternity-linked claim; hospital/discharge record; child Aadhaar only if the current portal requests it despite the 2025 simplification; proof of birth order/previous children; nominee or guardian documents in an exceptional case.
schemes.application_mode: Online through Punjab Kirti Sahayak or the Punjab BOCW portal, with district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner assistance; the official Form 46 is also published for Sewa Kendra/by-post/manual processing.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm active registration and contribution record. 2) Select Maternity Benefit in Kirti Sahayak/BOCW or obtain Form 46. 3) Enter worker, delivery, child and bank details. 4) Upload the registered birth certificate, identity/bank proof and declaration. 5) Submit promptly and save the acknowledgement. 6) Respond to Labour Department objections and track DBT payment.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No current official deadline was exposed in the reviewed live pages; older form guidance should be checked against the portal. Submit immediately after birth and verify any current one-year or shorter claim window. Benefit is one-time per eligible birth, up to two children.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Use https://bocw1.punjab.gov.in/bapi/worker/status with registration number, Aadhaar or mobile; escalate to district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner, Punjab BOCW head office Labour Bhawan Sector 64 Mohali (0172-2702486/0172-2211755) and the Labour Department.

schemes.scheme_name: Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board Pension and Family Pension
schemes.administering_body: Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Department of Labour, Government of Punjab; district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner and pension-record/payment authorities
schemes.benefit_summary: Monthly pension from age 60 based on membership duration, revised with effect from 1 December 2025: Rs 1,000 for 3 years’ membership, Rs 1,500 for 3–7 years, Rs 2,000 for 7–10 years and Rs 3,000 for more than 10 years. Eligible family pension is Rs 500, Rs 750, Rs 1,000 or Rs 1,500 respectively. Existing pensioners and workers eligible by 30 November 2025 retain the then-applicable Rs 3,000/Rs 1,500 rates under the circular.
schemes.eligibility_text: Registered construction worker who reaches 60 years and satisfies the Board membership/contribution requirement; current circular grades the amount by at least three years of membership. Family pension is payable to the eligible spouse/family member after the pensioner’s death under Board rules. The older official pension register form requires registration number, total membership, date of completing 60, spouse details and pension payment order. A life certificate is to be submitted in January each year to continue payment.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm whether the worker must cease construction work, the exact membership-date inclusivity at 3/7/10 years, contribution arrears/grace-period treatment, spouse priority and remarriage/dependency rules, and current digital life-certificate method. The 2026 circular’s grandfathering wording creates different rates for existing and newly eligible pensioners.
schemes.exclusions_text: Worker below 60; insufficient or unverified membership; inactive/lapsed contributions not regularised; duplicate or already sanctioned pension where rules prohibit it; ineligible spouse/family claimant; failure to submit annual life certificate; and false/incomplete registration or bank records.
schemes.documents_required: BOCW registration number; age/date-of-birth proof; evidence of membership/contributions; bank account/passbook; spouse details and identity; pension application/Form 44 or current online equivalent; photographs and self-declaration where requested.
schemes.conditional_documents: Pension Payment Order; death certificate and legal-heir/relationship proof for family pension; spouse non-remarriage/dependency certificate if required; annual life certificate; arrears/renewal receipts; guardian documents for a minor or dependent claimant.
schemes.application_mode: Online through Punjab BOCW portal/Kirti Sahayak where available, or through the prescribed pension form at a Sewa Kendra/by post/district Labour office. Government Services Portal lists separate ‘Pension Benefit’ and ‘Maintaining Pension Record’ services.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm registration duration and contribution status. 2) Around/after age 60, select Pension Benefit or obtain the current pension form. 3) Enter registration, age, membership, spouse and bank details. 4) Upload age, membership, identity and bank proof. 5) Submit to the portal/Sewa Kendra/district Labour office and retain acknowledgement. 6) Obtain/record the Pension Payment Order. 7) Submit life certificate every January and update the Board if family-pension circumstances change.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Apply on reaching 60; no annual fresh application once sanctioned, but life certificate is required every January. A current pension circular dated 8 January 2026 applies revised rates from 1 December 2025 and preserves older pensioners’ rates.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Check BOCW worker/file status at https://bocw1.punjab.gov.in/bapi/worker/status; ask the district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner about PPO and life-certificate status; escalate to BOCW head office Labour Bhawan Sector 64 Mohali and Labour Department.

schemes.scheme_name: Punjab BOCW Funeral and Last-Rites Assistance
schemes.administering_body: Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Department of Labour, Government of Punjab; district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner
schemes.benefit_summary: Rs 20,000 toward cremation/funeral expenses in Punjab for the death of a registered construction worker or an eligible family member. The registered worker may claim after a family member’s death; the nominee may claim after the worker’s death; an eligible family member may claim if both worker and nominee have died.
schemes.eligibility_text: Worker must be registered with the Punjab BOCW Board on the date of death. The death may be that of the worker or a covered family member. Claim must be made within one year of the death. The current Board handbook specifies Rs 20,000 for cremation within Punjab and the 2020 official Form 39 is the published application form.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm the exact definition/list of covered family members, whether cremation outside Punjab is excluded or merely needs special approval, nominee versus family-member priority, and whether one claim is allowed per death or per family. Verify any changed deadline in the live portal.
schemes.exclusions_text: Unregistered worker at death; death outside covered family relationship; cremation/funeral not covered by current Board rules; late or duplicate claim; missing death or identity evidence; and false/incomplete nominee or bank information.
schemes.documents_required: BOCW registration/member number; death certificate; Aadhaar/identity of deceased and applicant; proof of relationship or nomination; bank passbook/cancelled cheque; funeral/cremation details; self-declaration; Form 39 or online equivalent.
schemes.conditional_documents: Nominee certificate; legal-heir/family relationship and death certificate of a deceased nominee; proof of cremation within Punjab; guardian documents where claimant is a minor; any local authority/Gram Panchayat certificate requested for family relationship.
schemes.application_mode: Online through Punjab Kirti Sahayak/BOCW portal; the Government of India Services Portal lists the Punjab funeral-rites service as fully online. Form 39 and district Labour/Sewa Kendra assistance remain available for manual filing.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm active BOCW registration and identify nominee/family claimant. 2) Select Funeral/Last Rites Assistance in the portal or obtain Form 39. 3) Enter death, relationship, funeral and bank information. 4) Upload death certificate, identity, relationship/nominee proof and bank details. 5) Submit within one year and retain the acknowledgement. 6) Answer any Labour Department objection and track DBT payment.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Within one year of the death of the worker or covered family member. One-time assistance per eligible death; no annual renewal.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Use https://bocw1.punjab.gov.in/bapi/worker/status with registration number, Aadhaar or mobile; escalate to district Labour Inspector/Assistant Labour Commissioner, BOCW head office Labour Bhawan Sector 64 Mohali and Punjab Labour Department.

schemes.scheme_name: Chandigarh Hamari Beti Scheme (girl-child benefit; not Ladli Lakshmi)
schemes.administering_body: Department of Social Welfare, Women and Child Development, Chandigarh Administration; ICDS Child Development Project Officer-III / Joint Director / Director Social Welfare
schemes.benefit_summary: For eligible priority-household families, Rs 40,000 is placed in a fixed deposit in a joint account in the girl child’s and Programme Officer’s names. The Ministry of Home Affairs’ 2025-26 Chandigarh report says the FD is initially for five years and renewed/extended to maximise benefit during an 18-year retention period. The official ServicePlus service provides an output certificate/report.
schemes.eligibility_text: The current Chandigarh ServicePlus entry identifies Hamari Beti as an online citizen scheme requiring proof of the place/hospital/dispensary of birth, the girl child’s birth certificate, a Priority Household ration card and Chandigarh residence proof. The girl-child birth and family must satisfy the scheme’s priority-household and UT residence rules; institutional-delivery evidence is requested. The scheme should not be confused with Madhya Pradesh’s Ladli Lakshmi Yojana, which was not found as a Chandigarh scheme.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Confirm current age/birth cut-off, whether the girl must be born in Chandigarh or only reside there, whether the benefit is limited to the first/second girl, retention/withdrawal conditions at 18, and whether the Priority Household definition or FD amount has changed since the current annual report. The 2020 RTI budget entry is stale, but ServicePlus and the 2025-26 MHA report confirm the scheme exists.
schemes.exclusions_text: Non-priority-household family; non-Chandigarh residence where UT residence is required; missing birth/place-of-birth proof; duplicate claim; unregistered birth; false ration-card/residence information; and any girl-child case outside current age/birth-order rules.
schemes.documents_required: Girl child’s birth certificate; hospital/dispensary discharge slip or other place-of-birth proof; Priority Household ration card; parent/applicant Aadhaar or other residence proof such as voter ID, passport, driving licence, telephone/electricity bill or bank passbook; online registration details.
schemes.conditional_documents: Guardian/relationship proof; girl-child Aadhaar; immunisation or Anganwadi enrolment evidence if the current ICDS form requests it; bank/FD details and any appeal documents for delayed birth registration.
schemes.application_mode: Online through Chandigarh ServicePlus, service ID 16320002, with citizen registration; route may also be assisted through an e-Sampark/ICDS centre if the applicant needs help.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Register/login at ServicePlus. 2) Select Chandigarh Social Welfare/WCD and Hamari Beti. 3) Enter parent, girl-child, residence and priority-household details. 4) Upload birth certificate, institutional-delivery/place proof, ration card and residence proof. 5) Submit and save the application/acknowledgement. 6) Monitor the output certificate/report and contact ICDS/CDPO-III for defects or FD status.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: ServicePlus lists a 60-day Right to Service period; no separate annual application deadline was found. Registration should be made as soon as possible after birth and before any current age/birth cut-off.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track in ServicePlus using the application number; use Chandigarh Administration RTSC/ServicePlus grievance channels or contact Director Social Welfare, Town Hall Extension Building Sector 17 (0172-2700372, dswsec17-chd@nic.in) and the concerned ICDS CDPO.

The surviving household/head or eligible dependent applies with death, BPL, age, residence, relationship and bank proof.
