schemes.scheme_name: Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Students Belonging to Minority Communities (Chandigarh applicants)
schemes.jurisdiction: Chandigarh UT routing through the National Scholarship Portal
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India; Chandigarh Administration/institution nodal verification authorities; National Scholarship Portal
schemes.benefit_summary: Scholarship for students from the six notified minority communities—Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain and Parsi—studying from Class XI through PhD, including recognised technical/vocational courses. Historical official scheme materials provide admission/tuition fee support and maintenance allowance by course/group; the exact current amount table must be taken from the live scheme specification.
schemes.eligibility_text: Indian student belonging to one of the six notified minority communities; studying in a recognised school/college/institute/ITI in post-matric or post-secondary study from Class XI to PhD; at least 50% marks or equivalent grade in the previous final examination; annual parental/guardian income not exceeding Rs 2 lakh under the Ministry’s scheme guidance; and generally not receiving another scholarship/stipend. Only two children per family were stated in the official FAQ/guidance, subject to current rules. Chandigarh applicants also need the residential/domicile proof required by the scheme and institution/UT verification.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The 2026-27 NSP listing reviewed does not show a Ministry of Minority Affairs Post-Matric Scholarship card, so current opening status, revised income ceiling, amount table, two-child rule and Chandigarh nodal workflow are unresolved. Confirm whether the scheme is temporarily unavailable, migrated to another portal or opened later in the academic cycle; do not assume the historical Rs 2 lakh ceiling has changed or remains unchanged.
schemes.exclusions_text: Non-notified minority community; income above the applicable ceiling; previous marks below the threshold; unrecognised course/institution; duplicate scholarship/stipend; more than two family beneficiaries where current rules retain that cap; incomplete community/income/residence/bank records; and a closed or unavailable NSP cycle.
schemes.documents_required: Student photograph; institution verification form; income certificate or self-declaration as required by the current scheme; community certificate/self-declaration; previous academic marksheet; current-course fee receipt; student bank-account proof; residential certificate; Aadhaar where requested; admission/course/institution details.
schemes.conditional_documents: Renewal marksheet and previous scholarship ID; Chandigarh domicile/residence proof; hostel certificate; disability or other special-category proof only if a linked benefit is claimed; hard-copy documents required by the institution or Chandigarh nodal officer.
schemes.application_mode: The official Minority Affairs scheme guidance mandates online application through the National Scholarship Portal for fresh and renewal claims, with institution and state/UT verification. Current 2026 NSP availability must be checked before attempting a submission.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Ask the institution scholarship nodal officer whether the Minority Affairs PMS scheme is visible for AY 2026-27. 2) Complete NSP One-Time Registration if the scheme is open. 3) Select the Minority Affairs post-matric scheme, enter community, income, course, residence and bank details. 4) Upload the current checklist and final-submit. 5) Provide printout/documents to the institution if required. 6) Track institute/UT/ministry verification and resolve defects; if the scheme is absent, contact Minority Affairs/NSP helpdesk rather than submitting under a different scheme.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No 2026-27 student deadline was verified because the current NSP scheme listing did not display the Minority Affairs PMS card. Historical applications generally opened during the academic session and required fresh/renewal selection; follow only the current NSP/Ministry notice.
schemes.tracking_grievance: If visible on NSP, track with OTR/application login and institution/state nodal officer. NSP helpdesk: 0120-6619540 and helpdesk@nsp.gov.in; PFMS helpdesk 1800-118-111 where payment is the issue. For scheme-policy questions contact Ministry of Minority Affairs and Chandigarh Education/Social Welfare nodal offices.

schemes.scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)
schemes.jurisdiction: India; participating banks and Business Correspondent/Bank Mitra outlets
schemes.administering_body: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance; participating banks and Bank Mitras
schemes.benefit_summary: Basic Savings Bank Deposit account for an unbanked adult with no minimum-balance requirement, interest on deposits, RuPay debit card with accident insurance (₹2 lakh for new accounts opened after 28 August 2018), DBT access and possible overdraft up to ₹10,000 subject to eligibility. Insurance/overdraft benefits are conditional, not automatic cash grants.
schemes.eligibility_text: The current DFS page focuses on opening one basic account for an unbanked adult/person who does not already have another bank account. An account can be opened at a bank branch or Bank Mitra/Business Correspondent outlet. Minors and other low-risk customers may be handled under normal bank/minor-account/KYC rules, but the PMJDY benefit package must be confirmed with the bank.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The bank must determine whether the applicant is unbanked, complete KYC and issue/activate the RuPay card. Overdraft eligibility requires satisfactory operation and other bank conditions; accident cover requires a valid RuPay card and qualifying transaction/terms. Do not promise life insurance or overdraft solely from opening an account.
schemes.exclusions_text: A person with an existing bank account may not qualify for a new PMJDY BSBD account under the intended unbanked route. Incomplete/invalid KYC, duplicate accounts, inoperative accounts or failure to satisfy RuPay/overdraft conditions can block individual benefits. Bank account services remain subject to RBI/bank rules.
schemes.documents_required: Aadhaar/Aadhaar number where available; if unavailable, an officially valid document such as voter ID, driving licence, PAN, passport or MGNREGA card. Current-address self-certification may suffice where Aadhaar address differs. Mobile number and nominee details should be provided for banking/DBT.
schemes.conditional_documents: For low-risk customers without standard OVD, a government/PSU/bank photo ID or gazetted-officer certified letter may be accepted under KYC rules. For minors/guardians, guardian KYC and birth/age proof apply. RuPay activation and accident-claim documents are conditional.
schemes.application_mode: Assisted/offline at any participating bank branch or Bank Mitra/Business Correspondent; banks may also offer digital account opening. The official PMJDY site supplies English/Hindi account-opening forms and bank links.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Check that the applicant is unbanked and choose a participating bank/Bank Mitra. 2) Carry Aadhaar/OVD, mobile and nominee details. 3) Complete the PMJDY/BSBD account form and KYC. 4) Receive account number/passbook and RuPay card; activate the card. 5) Ask the bank specifically about DBT seeding, overdraft eligibility and qualifying RuPay transaction requirements. 6) Save the bank's acknowledgement and use the official helpline for unresolved issues.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No application deadline or annual renewal for the account. Keep KYC, mobile, nominee and address updated; overdraft, card and insurance benefits depend on continuing account/card conditions.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Contact the branch/Bank Mitra, the DFS PMJDY helplines 1800-11-0001 or 1800-180-1111, and use the bank's grievance channel. For RuPay insurance claims, follow the issuing bank/RuPay claim process.
schemes.source_authority: Department of Financial Services/PMJDY official pages and participating bank KYC records

schemes.scheme_name: Sukanya Samriddhi Account (SSA) Scheme
schemes.jurisdiction: India; authorized post offices and authorized commercial bank branches
schemes.administering_body: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance; India Post and authorized commercial banks
schemes.benefit_summary: Government small-savings account opened in the name of a resident Indian girl child below age 10 by a natural/legal guardian. Minimum opening/subsequent deposit is ₹250 (multiples of ₹50); annual deposit range is ₹250 to ₹1.5 lakh. Account matures 21 years from opening, with permitted education withdrawal up to 50% after age 18/10th standard and marriage closure subject to rules. Interest rate is notified quarterly and must be checked in the current notification.
schemes.eligibility_text: A guardian may open one account for a girl child who has not attained age 10 on the opening date and who is a resident Indian citizen. Normally one account per girl child and a maximum of two girl children per family/guardian are permitted, subject to the exceptions in the current rules. The girl remains eligible only while the residency/citizenship and account rules are satisfied.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: The authorized post office/bank must apply the current SSA rules on twin/triplet exceptions, guardianship, resident status, default restoration, premature closure and interest rate. An NRI/non-resident status change must be reported and can affect continuation; account opening is not a general adult savings route.
schemes.exclusions_text: A girl aged 10 or above at opening, non-resident/non-citizen beneficiary, duplicate account for the same girl, or account beyond the family-account limit is not eligible except for notified exceptions. Deposits above the annual limit, missing annual minimum deposit and unauthorised withdrawals follow default/irregular-account rules rather than creating additional benefit.
schemes.documents_required: SSA account-opening form, girl child's birth certificate (mandatory under India Post guidance), guardian KYC/address proof and photograph, girl child's Aadhaar/PAN if available, and initial deposit of at least ₹250. Provide bank/post-office account details for later deposits and guardian relationship information.
schemes.conditional_documents: Legal guardianship/adoption proof, twin/triplet birth evidence, resident-status/citizenship information, PAN/Aadhaar/address update and marriage/education/medical documents for permitted withdrawal/closure are conditional on the case.
schemes.application_mode: Assisted/offline account opening at an authorized post office or authorized commercial bank branch; deposits can later be made through approved channels including India Post/IPPB where supported. There is no central online eligibility application.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Confirm the girl is below 10 and resident Indian and that no duplicate/family-limit account exists. 2) Obtain birth certificate, guardian KYC and account-opening form. 3) Submit at the post office/authorized bank with at least ₹250. 4) Receive passbook/account number and make at least the annual minimum deposit by 31 March. 5) Use the account's permitted education withdrawal/closure process with supporting documents when eligible. 6) Update status/address and monitor government-notified interest rates.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Account opening has no annual deadline while the child is below 10, but at least ₹250 must be deposited each financial year (1 April–31 March) to keep the account regular. Maturity is 21 years from opening; deposits are generally required for 15 years under the scheme rules.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track through the post-office/bank passbook and branch. Escalate to India Post or the bank's savings grievance officer; scheme rules/notified rates are issued by the Department of Economic Affairs and India Post.
schemes.source_authority: India Post official SSA rules/manual and Department of Economic Affairs notifications; authorized bank/post-office records control account opening
schemes.next_review_action: Verify the latest quarterly interest rate, current SSA account form, authorized bank list and any updated twin/triplet/residency rules before user-facing deployment.

schemes.scheme_name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme
schemes.jurisdiction: India; commercial banks, Regional Rural Banks, cooperative banks and small finance banks
schemes.administering_body: Reserve Bank of India/NABARD framework, implemented by participating banks and cooperatives; Government interest-subvention/prompt-repayment terms apply when notified
schemes.benefit_summary: Single-window revolving credit for crop cultivation, post-harvest/marketing and household needs, maintenance of farm assets and allied agriculture, plus term-loan investment. Limit is assessed from area, crop/scale of finance, post-harvest and farm-maintenance components and investment need; small/marginal farmers may receive a flexible composite limit. Interest subsidy and prompt-repayment incentive are policy-year and lender dependent.
schemes.eligibility_text: Eligible applicants include individual or joint owner cultivators; tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers; and SHGs/JLGs of farmers including tenant/sharecropper groups. The bank assesses cultivation/insurable interest, land or tenancy evidence, crop pattern, repayment capacity and any term-loan proposal.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: Exact limit, interest rate, subsidy, collateral threshold, land-record/tenant proof and renewal period vary by bank, State and current RBI/Government instructions. KCC is a bank credit product, not a guaranteed entitlement; farmers without formal land title need the bank's accepted tenancy/JLG route.
schemes.exclusions_text: Applicants without demonstrable cultivation/allied-activity interest, false/duplicate land or crop declarations, unacceptable repayment risk, overdue defaults or missing KYC/bank documents may be declined. Collateral/security can be required above applicable no-collateral thresholds under current bank/RBI policy; insurance is not automatically included unless selected/notified.
schemes.documents_required: KCC application form, identity/address proof (Aadhaar, voter ID, driving licence/passport), two photographs, bank account details, landholding record certified by revenue authority, crop/area and cultivation details, and proof of tenancy/lease/sharecropping where applicable.
schemes.conditional_documents: KCC/JLG/SHG resolution, land lease or cultivation certificate, crop-sowing/scale-of-finance evidence, quotations for term-loan assets, existing loan statements, insurance/nominee details and collateral/security documents are conditional on limit, activity and lender.
schemes.application_mode: Online application on a participating bank's website where offered, or offline at a bank branch, cooperative/PACS, RRB or Business Correspondent. The official RBI framework leaves operational adaptation to implementing banks.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Choose a participating bank/cooperative and identify crop/allied activity and area. 2) Prepare KYC, land/tenancy/cultivation and bank documents. 3) Submit KCC application online or at the branch/PACS/BC. 4) Complete field/land verification and credit appraisal; negotiate limit, drawing power, collateral and repayment terms. 5) Receive the electronic KCC/smart debit card and operate within the sanctioned limit. 6) Renew/review the limit and make prompt repayment to preserve eligibility for any current subsidy/incentive.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: No national enrollment deadline; applications are ongoing, but crop-season disbursement, renewal and interest-subsidy cut-offs are bank/State/policy-year dependent. KCC limits are commonly reviewed over a multi-year period, with annual drawing limits and crop-season repayment dates.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track with the sanctioning bank/branch, KCC account and BC/PACS. Escalate to the bank's grievance officer, controlling office, RBI Integrated Ombudsman where applicable, NABARD/State-level banking committee or agriculture department for implementation issues.
schemes.source_authority: RBI official KCC master circular and NABARD/bank implementation materials; sanctioning bank's current policy controls the individual loan
schemes.next_review_action: For pilot States, capture the current KCC application forms, participating banks/PACS, tenant/sharecropper proof, collateral thresholds, interest-subvention terms and grievance contacts.

schemes.scheme_name: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme / Apprenticeship India candidate route
schemes.jurisdiction: India; apprenticeshipindia.gov.in with establishments and Regional/State Apprenticeship Advisers under the Apprentices Act framework
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Directorate General of Training/Apprenticeship Advisers; NAPS portal facilitates candidate/establishment registration, contracts and employer reimbursements
schemes.benefit_summary: Candidates register on the central Apprenticeship India portal, search establishment opportunities by State, district, trade and sector, apply to vacancies and, if selected, enter a formal apprenticeship contract for on-the-job and classroom training. The apprentice receives the notified employer stipend; NAPS reimbursement is primarily an employer-side support and is not an assured candidate cash grant.
schemes.eligibility_text: Eligibility is vacancy/trade specific. The official candidate route supports ITI/skill-course pass-outs, graduates/diploma holders, candidates pursuing graduation/diploma and other eligible fresh apprentices; NSDC states minimum education can start at 5th class for relevant categories. Candidate must satisfy the advertised trade, age, qualification, medical and prior-apprenticeship conditions, and the establishment's vacancy rules.
schemes.eligibility_unresolved: There is no single age/qualification rule for every trade or establishment. Individual vacancy notices determine age cut-off, passed-out period, medical fitness, prior job/apprenticeship experience, reservation, domicile and document list. NAPS portal registration alone does not create a placement or stipend entitlement.
schemes.exclusions_text: A candidate may be ineligible for a particular vacancy if under the stated minimum age, awaiting required result, lacking the advertised qualification, medically unfit, already completed/undertaking prohibited prior apprenticeship or exceeding experience limits. False documents, duplicate profiles or failure to sign the contract/attend verification can cancel selection.
schemes.documents_required: Valid email/mobile, Aadhaar or other portal identity details, date-of-birth/10th certificate, education/ITI/diploma/degree marksheets and certificates, photograph, signature, bank details and category/disability/EWS documents where the vacancy asks. Some employers require PAN and Aadhaar-linked bank account.
schemes.conditional_documents: Medical fitness certificate, domicile/residence, caste/OBC-NCL/EWS certificate, disability certificate, NAPS/NATS registration number, employment exchange or establishment-specific forms and original-document verification are conditional on the advertised apprenticeship.
schemes.application_mode: Online candidate registration and vacancy application at https://www.apprenticeshipindia.gov.in/. Candidates must activate the account by email, complete the profile, search opportunities and apply individually; employers may also require a second application on their recruitment portal.
schemes.application_steps: 1) Open Apprenticeship India and choose Register > Candidate. 2) Enter basic/family/contact details and activate through the email link. 3) Complete the profile with Aadhaar, education, trade, bank and documents. 4) Search opportunities by State/district/sector/trade and read each vacancy notice. 5) Apply before that establishment's deadline, preserving registration/application number. 6) Attend merit/document/medical verification, sign the apprenticeship contract if selected and track joining/stipend through the establishment/portal.
schemes.deadline_or_renewal: Candidate registration is generally ongoing, but each establishment vacancy has its own opening/closing dates and qualification cut-off. There is no single national candidate deadline. A new application is required for each opportunity; training duration and contract renewal depend on the trade/establishment.
schemes.tracking_grievance: Track profile, applications and contracts on the Apprenticeship India portal; contact apprenticeship@nsdcindia.org for portal support and the relevant Regional/State Apprenticeship Adviser for statutory issues. The establishment is the first contact for selection, joining, stipend and attendance disputes.
schemes.source_authority: NSDC/Apprenticeship India official candidate guidance and government apprenticeship-adviser portals; each employer's current vacancy notice controls selection
schemes.next_review_action: Verify live portal accessibility, candidate manual, current NAPS/NATS distinction, pilot-region apprenticeship advisers and a sample of active openings before promising any specific placement.
